# Palette Animation Investigation in Room 7 (2026-02-02 20:25Z)

_**User (2026-02-02 21:15Z)**_

in room 7, when using object number 7 (the amulet) in the hotspot 353 (the statue), theres a palette animation happening that transforms the colors of the statue into something more reddish, through a fade effect in multiple colors. Then a conversation triggers with the only character in the room (the starting root 1, so the second one for this npc), the palette reverts back to the original.  I dont believe this is a different palette, just a palette fade on multiple colors. The effect blocks the entire game interaction so it must be in its own loop, not even the mouse can be seen moving.

We have not identified a palette animation so far in room 7. I need you to see where this animation comes from and how it is applied. The palette before the animation, as extracted from a Dosbox raw screenshot is:

Note these are 8-bit palettes vs 6-bit that the game uses! They are palettes for the normal and final state of the animation; in reality there are multiple in-between states, since the effect is a fade. Not all colors are affected by this fade.

Please analyze the ghidra code and try to figure out how to apply this effect as well. There are some docs on the dispatch tables for actions and item combinations (this case) but i dont know how reliable they are. 

Do not use heredoc python. Clean up all the temp scripts after yourself. Rename functions and vars on ghidra as you go.

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Find the amulet+statue (353+7) handler in the item combination table.\"\"\"\nimport struct\n\nwith open('files/JUEGO.EXE', 'rb') as f:\n    data = f.read()\n\n# Item table at file offset 0x4B318 (memory 0x48118)\ntable_offset = 0x4B318\nprint(\"Searching for entries matching hotspot 353 or item 7...\")\nprint(\"Entry format: 8 bytes [hotspot_extra_id: 2, item_id: 2, func_ptr: 4]\")\nprint()\n\nfor i in range(200):\n    entry_offset = table_offset + i * 8\n    entry = data[entry_offset:entry_offset+8]\n    if len(entry) &lt; 8:\n        break\n    item1, item2, func = struct.unpack('&lt;HHI', entry)\n    if item1 == 0xFFFF:\n        print(f\"Table terminator at entry {i}\")\n        break\n    if item1 == 353 or item2 == 353 or item1 == 7 or item2 == 7:\n        print(f\"Entry {i} @ 0x{entry_offset:X}: item1={item1} (0x{item1:X}), item2={item2} (0x{item2:X}), func=0x{func:X}\")\n",
  "toolCallResult": null
}

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nSearch for palette index tables in JUEGO.EXE that match the statue animation colors.\n\"\"\"\nimport struct\n\n# Palette indices that change: 30, 37, 39, 41, 44, 62, 74, 79, 89, 105, 152, 217, 238\nindices = [30, 37, 39, 41, 44, 62, 74, 79, 89, 105, 152, 217, 238]\nindices_set = set(indices)\n\nwith open('files/JUEGO.EXE', 'rb') as f:\n    data = f.read()\n\nprint(\"Searching for palette index tables...\")\nprint(f\"Target indices: {indices}\")\nprint(f\"As hex: {[hex(x) for x in indices]}\")\nprint()\n\n# Search for these bytes appearing consecutively\nsearch_bytes = bytes(indices)\nprint(f\"Searching for consecutive indices as bytes...\")\n\npos = data.find(search_bytes)\nif pos != -1:\n    print(f\"Found exact sequence at file offset 0x{pos:X}\")\nelse:\n    print(\"Exact sequence not found as consecutive bytes\")\n\nprint()\n\n# Search for a table where indices appear in some structured format\n# Common formats: [index, R, G, B] or [index, target_R, target_G, target_B]\n# Or just [index] followed by color data\n\nprint(\"Searching for scattered index matches in data tables...\")\nmatches = []\n\nfor i in range(len(data) - 50):\n    found_count = 0\n    found_positions = []\n    \n    # Check 50 byte window for our indices\n    for j in range(min(50, len(data) - i)):\n        if data[i + j] in indices_set:\n            found_count += 1\n            found_positions.append((j, data[i + j]))\n    \n    if found_count &gt;= 6:  # At least 6 of our 13 indices\n        # Filter to show only interesting patterns\n        mem_addr = i - 0x3200 if i &gt;= 0x3200 else i\n        matches.append((i, mem_addr, found_count, found_positions[:10]))\n\n# Show only top matches\nmatches.sort(key=lambda x: -x[2])\nprint(f\"Found {len(matches)} regions with 6+ matching indices\")\nprint()\n\nfor file_off, mem_addr, count, positions in matches[:5]:\n    print(f\"File offset 0x{file_off:X} (mem ~0x{mem_addr:X}): {count} matches\")\n    print(f\"  Bytes: {data[file_off:file_off+50].hex(' ')}\")\n    print(f\"  Matches: {positions}\")\n    print()\n\n# Also search for specific patterns like room 7 checks\nprint(\"Searching for room 7 (0x07) comparisons near palette code...\")\nfor i in range(len(data) -   "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nSearch for the target palette colors in the game executable.\nThe animation fades FROM original TO target colors.\n\"\"\"\nimport struct\n\n# Target colors (6-bit VGA values, converted from 8-bit)\n# Entry | After 8-bit -&gt; 6-bit\n#   30  | D7,8A,5D -&gt; 35,22,17\n#   37  | FB,9E,0C -&gt; 3E,27,03\n#   39  | BA,14,04 -&gt; 2E,05,01\n#   41  | 24,0C,00 -&gt; 09,03,00\n#   44  | C3,59,3C -&gt; 30,16,0F\n#   62  | 79,41,65 -&gt; 1E,10,19\n#   74  | FF,AE,41 -&gt; 3F,2B,10\n#   79  | F3,65,00 -&gt; 3C,19,00\n#   89  | FF,9A,51 -&gt; 3F,26,14\n#  105  | 00,00,00 -&gt; 00,00,00\n#  152  | 6D,18,51 -&gt; 1B,06,14\n#  217  | 75,14,00 -&gt; 1D,05,00\n#  238  | CB,34,1C -&gt; 32,0D,07\n\n# Target colors in 6-bit VGA format (R, G, B)\ntarget_colors_6bit = [\n    (0x35, 0x22, 0x17),  # Entry 30\n    (0x3E, 0x27, 0x03),  # Entry 37\n    (0x2E, 0x05, 0x01),  # Entry 39\n    (0x09, 0x03, 0x00),  # Entry 41\n    (0x30, 0x16, 0x0F),  # Entry 44\n    (0x1E, 0x10, 0x19),  # Entry 62\n    (0x3F, 0x2B, 0x10),  # Entry 74\n    (0x3C, 0x19, 0x00),  # Entry 79\n    (0x3F, 0x26, 0x14),  # Entry 89\n    (0x00, 0x00, 0x00),  # Entry 105\n    (0x1B, 0x06, 0x14),  # Entry 152\n    (0x1D, 0x05, 0x00),  # Entry 217\n    (0x32, 0x0D, 0x07),  # Entry 238\n]\n\nindices = [30, 37, 39, 41, 44, 62, 74, 79, 89, 105, 152, 217, 238]\n\nwith open('files/JUEGO.EXE', 'rb') as f:\n    data = f.read()\n\nprint(\"Searching for target palette color tables...\")\nprint()\n\n# Build a search pattern: [index, R, G, B] repeated\n# Or possibly: [R, G, B, R, G, B, ...] with separate index table\n\n# First, let's search for specific distinctive RGB values\n# Entry 37: FB,9E,0C (8-bit) or 3E,27,03 (6-bit) - very distinctive\n# Entry 74: FF,AE,41 (8-bit) or 3F,2B,10 (6-bit) - very distinctive\n# Entry 79: F3,65,00 (8-bit) or 3C,19,00 (6-bit) - distinctive\n\nprint(\"Searching for distinctive 6-bit color values...\")\nsearch_patterns = [\n    (bytes([0x3E, 0x27, 0x03]), \"Entry 37 target\"),\n    (bytes([0x3F, 0x2B, 0x10]), \"Entry 74 target\"),\n    (bytes([0x3C, 0x19, 0x00]), \"Entry 79 target\"),\n    (bytes([0x3F, 0x26, 0x14]), \"Entry 89 target\"),\n    (bytes([0x32, 0x0D, 0x07]), \"Entry 238 target\"),\n]\n\nfor pattern, desc in search_patterns:\n    pos = 0\n    while True:\n        pos = data.find(pattern, pos)\n        if pos == -1:\n            break\n        mem_addr = pos - 0x3200 if pos &gt;= 0x3200 else pos\n        # Show context\n        context = data[max(0,pos-10):pos+20]\n        print(f\"{desc} at file 0x{pos:X} (mem ~0x{mem_addr:X})\")\n        print(f\"  Context: {context.hex(' ')}\")\n        pos += 1\n\nprint()\nprint(\"Searching for table format [index, R, G, B]...\")\n# Look for patterns like: 1E R G B 25 R G B 27 R G B ...\nfor i in range(len(data) - 52):\n    # Check for 4-byte format: [index, R, G, B]\n    match_count = 0\n    matched_entries = []\n    for j, (idx, (r, g, b)) in enumerate(zip(indices[:5], target_colors_6bit[:5])):\n        offset = i + j * 4\n        if offset + 3 &lt; len(data):\n            if data[offset] == idx and data[offset+1] == r and data[offset+2] == g and data[offset+3] == b:\n                match_count += 1\n                matched_entries.append(idx)\n    \n    if match_count &gt;= 3:\n        mem_addr = i - 0x3200 if i &gt;= 0x3200 else i\n        print(f\"Possible 4-byte table at file 0x{i:X} (mem ~0x{mem_addr:X})\")\n        print(f\"  Matched entries: {matched_entries}\")\n        print(f\"  Bytes: {data[i:i+40].hex(' ')}\")\n\nprint()\nprint(\"Searching for table format [R, G, B] only (indices stored separately)...\")\n# Build RGB-only pattern\nrgb_pattern = b''.join(bytes([r, g, b]) for r, g, b in target_colors_6bit[:4])\nprint(f\"Looking for first 4 colors: {rgb_pattern.hex(' ')}\")\n\npos = data.find(rgb_pattern)\nif pos != -1:\n    print(f\"Found at file 0x{pos:X}\")\nelse:\n    print(\"Not found as consecutive RGB triplets\")\n",

    "original": "python3 -c \"\nimport struct\n\n# Search for references to the palette animation table addresses\n# Index table at 0x49508, source colors at 0x49518, target at 0x49548\n\nwith open('files/JUEGO.EXE', 'rb') as f:\n    data = f.read()\n\n# Search for these addresses as 32-bit values\ntargets = [0x49500, 0x49508, 0x49518, 0x49548, 0x4C700, 0x4C708, 0x4C718, 0x4C748]\n\nfor target in targets:\n    # Search for the address as little-endian 32-bit\n    pattern = struct.pack('&lt;I', target)\n    pos = 0\n    while True:\n        pos = data.find(pattern, pos)\n        if pos == -1:\n            break\n        mem_ref = pos - 0x3200 if pos &gt;= 0x3200 else pos\n        print(f'Reference to 0x{target:X} at file 0x{pos:X} (mem ~0x{mem_ref:X})')\n        pos += 1\n\n# Also search for offsets that could be used with a base pointer\n# The header had 0x170 and 0x94\nprint()\nprint('Searching for header values 0x170, 0x94 as references...')\nfor val in [0x170, 0x94]:\n    pattern = struct.pack('&lt;H', val)\n    found = 0\n    pos = 0\n    while found &lt; 5:\n        pos = data.find(pattern, pos)\n        if pos == -1:\n            break\n        # Only show if in code section\n        if 0x3200 &lt; pos &lt; 0x30000:\n            mem_ref = pos - 0x3200\n            print(f'  Value 0x{val:X} at file 0x{pos:X} (mem ~0x{mem_ref:X})')\n            found += 1\n        pos += 1\n\" 2&gt;&amp;1 | head -40",

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Search for code that references the palette animation data.\"\"\"\nimport struct\n\nwith open('files/JUEGO.EXE', 'rb') as f:\n    data = f.read()\n\n# Search for these addresses as 32-bit values\ntargets = [0x49500, 0x49508, 0x49518, 0x49548]\n\nprint(\"Searching for direct references to palette data addresses...\")\nfor target in targets:\n    pattern = struct.pack('&lt;I', target)\n    pos = 0\n    while True:\n        pos = data.find(pattern, pos)\n        if pos == -1:\n            break\n        mem_ref = pos - 0x3200 if pos &gt;= 0x3200 else pos\n        print(f'Reference to 0x{target:X} at file 0x{pos:X} (mem ~0x{mem_ref:X})')\n        pos += 1\n\nprint()\n\n# The palette animation might be implemented as part of a more generic routine\n# Let's search for code that does selective palette updates\n# Pattern: loop with outport 0x3C8/0x3C9 and palette index from table\n\n# Search for the conversation control code 0xF8 which triggers special effects\nprint(\"Searching for conversation control code 0xF8 handlers...\")\n# The F8 code in text data triggers special actions\n\n# Actually, let me search for the palette fade loop pattern\n# It would involve: loading palette index, reading RGB values, writing to VGA port\nprint()\nprint(\"Searching for palette fade code patterns...\")\n# Pattern: OUT to port 0x3C8 (palette index), then 3x OUT to 0x3C9 (RGB)\n# as bytes: BA C8 03 (MOV DX, 0x3C8) or direct outport call\n\n# Search for code that accesses multiple palette indices from our list\nfor idx in [30, 37, 39, 41]:  # First few indices\n    # MOV AL, idx pattern\n    pattern = bytes([0xB0, idx])  # MOV AL, imm8\n    pos = 0\n    found = 0\n    while found &lt; 3:\n        pos = data.find(pattern, pos)\n        if pos == -1:\n            break\n        if 0x3200 &lt; pos &lt; 0x30000:\n            mem_ref = pos - 0x3200\n            # Check context\n            context = data[pos-5:pos+10]\n            print(f'MOV AL, {idx} at file 0x{pos:X} (mem ~0x{mem_ref:X}): {context.hex(\" \")}')\n            found += 1\n        pos += 1\n",

delta = 0x3200\nfile_offset = 0x12CC1 + 0x3200\n\nprint(f\"Handler at memory 0x12CC1 (file 0x{file_offset:X})\")\nprint(\"=\" * 60)\n\n# Read raw bytes\nraw_bytes = data[file_offset:file_offset+64]\nprint(f\"First 64 bytes:\")\nfor i in range(0, 64, 16):\n    hex_part = raw_bytes[i:i+16].hex(' ')\n    print(f\"  +0x{i:02X}: {hex_part}\")\n\n# Try to identify what instruction this starts with\n# ff 30 = PUSH dword ptr [EAX]\nfirst_byte = raw_bytes[0]\nsecond_byte = raw_bytes[1]\nprint()\nprint(f\"First bytes: 0x{first_byte:02X} 0x{second_byte:02X}\")\n\n# ff 30 is PUSH [EAX] - this is mid-function\n# Let's find the function start by looking for a standard prologue\n\n# Search backwards for a function prologue\n# Common prologues: 55 (PUSH EBP), 53 (PUSH EBX), 6A (PUSH imm8)\nprint()\nprint(\"Searching backwards for function prologue...\")\nfor offset in range(file_offset, file_offset - 200, -1):\n    # Check for PUSH EBP; MOV EBP, ESP pattern (55 89 E5 or 55 8B EC)\n    if data[offset:offset+2] in [b'\\x55\\x89', b'\\x55\\x8b']:\n        mem_addr = offset - 0x3200\n        print(f\"Possible function start at file 0x{offset:X} (mem 0x{mem_addr:X})\")\n        print(f\"  Bytes: {data[offset:offset+20].hex(' ')}\")\n        break\n    # Check for PUSH imm8 followed by CALL (6A xx E8)\n    if data[offset] == 0x6A and data[offset+2] == 0xE8:\n        mem_addr = offset - 0x3200\n        print(f\"Possible function start at file 0x{offset:X} (mem 0x{mem_addr:X})\")\n        print(f\"  Bytes: {data[offset:offset+20].hex(' ')}\")\n        # Don't break, keep looking\n\n# Let's also check what Ghidra thinks the function boundary is\n# by looking at the item dispatch mechanism\nprint()\nprint(\"Analyzing the item combination dispatch...\")\n\n# The dispatcher at execute_complex_item_script_table does:\n# (*(code *)(&amp;PTR_LAB_0004811c)[(index &amp; 0xff) * 2])()\n# \n# For entry 6: index=6, so it accesses 0x4811c + 6*8 = 0x4814c\n# Wait, the format is 8 bytes per entry: [item1:2][item2:2][func_ptr:4]\n# The function pointer is at offset 4 within each entry\n\n# Entry 6 is at file 0x4B348:\n#   61 01 07 00 C1 2C 01 00\n#   item1=0x0161 (353), item2=0x0007 (7), func=0x00012CC1\n\n# So the function pointer 0x12CC1 IS correct\n# But 0x12CC1 seems to be in the middle of another function\n\n# Let's check what function contains 0x12CC1\n# Ghidra shows amulet_statue_handler_353_7 at 0x12F06\n# But the table points to 0x12CC1\n\n# Maybe the table offset calculation is wrong?\n# Let's verify the table structure again\ntable_file_offset = 0x4B318\nprint(f\"\\nItem table at file 0x{table_file_offset:X}:\")\nfor i in range(10):\n    entry_offset = table_file_offset + i * 8\n    entry = data[entry_offset:entry_offset+8]\n    item1, item2, func = struct.unpack('&lt;HHI', entry)\n    if item1 == 0xFFFF:\n        print(f\"  Entry {i}: TERMINATOR\")\n        break\n    print(f\"  Entry {i}: item1={item1}, item2={item2}, func=0x{func:X}\")\n",

  "content": "",
  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nAnalyze the handler at 0x12CC1 (statue palette fade)\n\"\"\"\nimport struct\n\nwith open('files/JUEGO.EXE', 'rb') as f:\n    exe = f.read()\n\nfile_base = 0x3200\n\n# The item combination table entry 6 points to 0x12CC1\nhandler_addr = 0x12CC1\nhandler_file_off = handler_addr + file_base\n\nprint(\"=\"*70)\nprint(\"HANDLER AT 0x12CC1 ANALYSIS\")\nprint(\"=\"*70)\nprint(f\"Memory address: 0x{handler_addr:05X}\")\nprint(f\"File offset: 0x{handler_file_off:05X}\")\nprint()\n\n# Print 256 bytes of the handler code\nprint(\"Handler code bytes:\")\nhandler = exe[handler_file_off:handler_file_off+256]\nfor i in range(0, len(handler), 16):\n    hex_str = ' '.join(f'{b:02X}' for b in handler[i:i+16])\n    ascii_str = ''.join(chr(b) if 32 &lt;= b &lt; 127 else '.' for b in handler[i:i+16])\n    print(f\"  {handler_file_off+i:05X}: {hex_str:48s} {ascii_str}\")\n\nprint()\nprint(\"=\"*70)\nprint(\"PALETTE TABLE AT FILE 0x4C700\")\nprint(\"=\"*70)\n\npal_offset = 0x4C700\npal_data = exe[pal_offset:pal_offset+128]\n\n# Parse the header\nheader = pal_data[0:8]\nx_coord = struct.unpack('&lt;H', header[0:2])[0]  \ny_coord = struct.unpack('&lt;H', header[2:4])[0]\neffect_type = struct.unpack('&lt;H', header[4:6])[0]\nprint(f\"Header: x={x_coord} (0x{x_coord:04X}), y={y_coord} (0x{y_coord:04X}), type={effect_type}\")\n\n# Parse the 16 palette indices at offset 8\nindices = list(pal_data[8:24])\nprint(f\"\\nPalette indices (16 entries at offset 0x4C708):\")\nprint(f\"  {indices}\")\nprint(f\"  Decimal: {[i for i in indices]}\")\n\n# Parse source colors (16 * 3 bytes = 48 bytes) at offset 0x18 from start\nsource_offset = 0x4C718\nsource_colors = []\nfor i in range(16):\n    off = source_offset - pal_offset + i*3\n    r, g, b = pal_data[off:off+3]\n    source_colors.append((r, g, b))\nprint(f\"\\nSource colors (at file 0x4C718):\")\nfor i, (r, g, b) in enumerate(source_colors):\n    print(f\"  Index {indices[i]:3d}: RGB({r:2d},{g:2d},{b:2d}) = #{r*4:02X}{g*4:02X}{b*4:02X}\")\n\n# Parse target colors (16 * 3 bytes) at offset 0x48 from start\ntarget_offset = 0x4C748\ntarget_colors = []\nfor i in range(16):\n    off = target_offset - pal_offset + i*3\n    r, g, b = pal_data[off:off+3]\n    target_colors.append((r, g, b))\nprint(f\"\\nTarget colors (at file 0x4C748):\")\nfor i, (r, g, b) in enumerate(target_colors):\n    print(f\"  Index {indices[i]:3d}: RGB({r:2d},{g:2d},{b:2d}) = #{r*4:02X}{g*4:02X}{b*4:02X}\")\n\n# Check for references to the palette table in the exe\nprint()\nprint(\"=\"*70)\nprint(\"SEARCHING FOR REFERENCES TO PALETTE TABLE ADDRESS\")\nprint(\"=\"*70)\n\n# Memory address of palette table is 0x49500 (file 0x4C700 - 0x3200 = 0x49500)\npal_mem_addr = 0x4C700 - 0x3200\nprint(f\"Palette table memory address: 0x{pal_mem_addr:05X}\")\n\n# Search for this address in the EXE\n# It might appear as:\n# - Direct reference: 00 95 04 00 (little endian for 0x00049500)\nsearch_bytes = struct.pack('&lt;I', pal_mem_addr)\nprint(f\"Searching for bytes: {search_bytes.hex()}\")\n\ncount = 0\npos = 0\nwhile True:\n    pos = exe.find(search_bytes, pos)\n    if pos == -1:\n        break\n    mem_addr = pos - 0x3200 if pos &gt;= 0x3200 else pos\n    print(f\"  Found at file 0x{pos:05X} (memory ~0x{mem_addr:05X})\")\n    count += 1\n    pos += 1\nprint(f\"Total references: {count}\")\n\n# Also search for palette index start address (0x49508)\nidx_addr = pal_mem_addr + 8\nprint(f\"\\nSearching for palette indices address 0x{idx_addr:05X}:\")\nsearch_bytes = struct.pack('&lt;I', idx_addr)\ncount = 0\npos = 0\nwhile True:\n    pos = exe.find(search_bytes, pos)\n    if pos == -1:\n        break\n    mem_addr = pos - 0x3200 if pos &gt;= 0x3200 else pos\n    print(f\"  Found at file 0x{pos:05X} (memory ~0x{mem_addr:05X})\")\n    count += 1\n    pos += 1\nprint(f\"Total references: {count}\")\n",
  "toolCallResult": null
}

{

  "textEditContent": "# Statue Palette Fade Animation System\n\n## Overview\n\nWhen the player uses the **amulet (item 7)** on the **statue (hotspot 353)** in room 7, a palette fade animation transforms the statue's colors from grayish tones to reddish/warm tones.\n\n## Key Addresses\n\n| Description | Memory Address | File Offset |\n|------------|----------------|-------------|\n| Palette table | 0x49500 | 0x4C700 |\n| Step counter | 0x95F4 | - (BSS) |\n| Step array | 0xFC94 | - (BSS) |\n| F8 handler (action 353) | 0x1215E | 0x1435E |\n| Palette fade code | 0x227B1-0x228B0 | 0x259B1-0x25AB0 |\n\n## Palette Table Structure (at 0x4C700)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nOffset  Size  Description\n------  ----  -----------\n0x00    2     X position (368)\n0x02    2     Y position (148)\n0x04    2     Type (2)\n0x06    2     Padding\n0x08    16    Palette indices to modify\n0x18    48    Source RGB values (16 colors × 3 bytes, 6-bit VGA)\n0x48    48    Target RGB values (16 colors × 3 bytes, 6-bit VGA)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Total size: 120 bytes (0x78)**\n\n## Modified Palette Indices\n\nThe animation modifies these 16 palette entries:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n[30, 37, 39, 41, 44, 62, 74, 79, 83, 89, 105, 120, 152, 179, 217, 238]\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Color Transformation\n\n| Index | Source (R,G,B) | Target (R,G,B) | Description |\n|-------|----------------|----------------|-------------|\n| 30 | (44,44,40) | (53,34,23) | Gray → Orange-brown |\n| 37 | (36,36,36) | (62,39,3) | Gray → Bright orange |\n| 39 | (16,16,16) | (46,5,1) | Dark gray → Dark red |\n| 41 | (20,20,20) | (9,3,0) | Gray → Near black |\n| 44 | (36,36,32) | (48,22,15) | Gray → Brown |\n| 62 | (28,32,28) | (30,16,25) | Gray-green → Purple-brown |\n| 74 | (32,32,32) | (63,43,16) | Gray → Golden |\n| 79 | (16,16,12) | (60,25,0) | Dark gray → Orange |\n| 83 | (16,20,20) | (16,20,20) | No change |\n| 89 | (52,52,44) | (63,38,20) | Light gray → Gold |\n| 105 | (12,12,12) | (0,0,0) | Dark → Black |\n| 120 | (36,40,40) | (36,40,40) | No change |\n| 152 | (45,44,40) | (27,6,20) | Gray → Dark magenta |\n| 179 | (48,52,44) | (48,52,44) | No change |\n| 217 | (24,24,24) | (29,5,0) | Gray → Dark orange |\n| 238 | (24,28,28) | (50,13,7) | Gray → Red-orange |\n\n*RGB values are 6-bit VGA (0-63). Multiply by 4 for 8-bit equivalents.*\n\n## Animation Mechanism\n\n### 1. Trigger\nWhen item 7 (amulet) is used on hotspot 353 (statue):\n- The F8 handler at &#96;0x1215E&#96; is called\n- It sets &#96;statue_palette_fade_counter&#96; at &#96;0x495C4&#96; to **13** (0x0D)\n\n### 2. Per-Frame Processing\nThe code at &#96;0x227B1-0x228B0&#96; contains 4 code snippets that:\n1. Wait/delay for 12 ticks\n2. Call palette step function with specific step indices\n3. Increment the frame counter at &#96;0x95F4&#96;\n4. When counter reaches 4, trigger conversation root 1\n\n### 3. Step Values\nEach snippet uses different palette step values:\n- **Snippet 1** (0x227B1): steps 0x4D (77), 0x6B (107)\n- **Snippet 2** (0x227FA): steps 0x4E (78)\n- **Snippet 3** (0x22839): steps 0x4F (79), 0x6C (108)\n- **Snippet 4** (0x22882): steps 0x50 (80), 0x6D (109)\n\nThese step values likely index into pre-computed interpolation tables.\n\n### 4. Completion\nWhen the frame counter reaches 4:\n- A function is called with parameters (EBX=2, EDX=1, EAX=0x1B)\n- This triggers conversation root 1 with the statue\n\n## Code Flow\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nUser: Use amulet on statue\n  │\n  ▼\nItem combination table lookup (353 + 7)\n  │\n  ▼\nF8 handler at 0x1215E\n  │\n  ├── Sets Alfred position\n  ├── Resets various state\n  └── Sets palette_fade_counter = 13\n  │\n  ▼\nPer-frame loop (4 iterations)\n  │\n  ├── Delay 12 ticks\n  ├── Apply palette step N\n  ├── Apply palette step M\n  ├── Increment counter at 0x95F4\n  └── Check if counter == 4\n  │\n  ▼\nTrigger conversation root 1\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Implementation Notes for ScummVM\n\n1. **Palette Interpolation**: The game uses pre-computed step values rather than real-time interpolation. The ScummVM implementation should:\n   - Read the palette table structure at room load\n   - Interpolate between source and target colors over the animation frames\n   - Apply changes to only the 16 specified palette indices\n\n2. **Timing**: Each frame waits for 12 timer ticks before applying the next palette step\n\n3. **Conversation Trigger**: After 4 iterations, conversation root 1 should be enabled\n\n4. **UI Blocking**: During the animation, the mouse cursor is hidden and player input is blocked\n\n## Related Files\n\n- &#96;JUEGO.EXE&#96;: Contains the code and palette table\n- &#96;ALFRED.1&#96;: Room 7 data (statue hotspot defined here)\n",
  "toolCallResult": null
}

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Find all code that references the statue fade counter at 0x95F4\"\"\"\nimport struct\n\ncounter_addr = 0x95F4  # Memory address of counter\n\nwith open('files/JUEGO.EXE', 'rb') as f:\n    f.seek(0)\n    data = f.read()\n\n# Convert to bytes for searching\ncounter_bytes = struct.pack('&lt;I', counter_addr)\n\nprint(f\"Searching for references to counter at 0x{counter_addr:05X}...\")\nprint()\n\n# Search for the 4-byte address pattern\nidx = 0x3200  # Start of code section\nwhile idx &lt; len(data):\n    pos = data.find(counter_bytes, idx)\n    if pos == -1:\n        break\n    \n    # Get context\n    start = max(0, pos - 10)\n    end = min(len(data), pos + 20)\n    context = data[start:end]\n    \n    mem_addr = pos - 0x3200\n    print(f\"Found at file 0x{pos:05X} (mem 0x{mem_addr:05X}):\")\n    \n    # Show bytes\n    hex_str = ' '.join(f'{b:02X}' for b in context)\n    offset_in_context = pos - start\n    print(f\"  Context: {hex_str}\")\n    print(f\"  Marker:  {' '*(offset_in_context*3)}^^^^^^^^^^^ here\")\n    \n    # Try to identify instruction\n    byte_before = data[pos-1] if pos &gt; 0 else 0\n    byte_before2 = data[pos-2] if pos &gt; 1 else 0\n    \n    if byte_before == 0x05 and byte_before2 == 0xFE:\n        print(\"  -&gt; INC byte ptr [0x95F4]\")\n    elif byte_before == 0x05 and byte_before2 == 0xA0:\n        print(\"  -&gt; MOV AL, [0x95F4]\") \n    elif byte_before == 0x05:\n        print(f\"  -&gt; Opcode prefix: {data[pos-2]:02X} {byte_before:02X}\")\n    else:\n        print(f\"  -&gt; Prefix byte: {byte_before:02X}\")\n    \n    print()\n    idx = pos + 1\n\n# Also search for CMP instructions with 0x95F4\nprint(\"Looking for larger patterns around 0x95F4...\")\n",
  "toolCallResult": null
}

  "content": "",
  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Decode call targets from palette fade code\"\"\"\nimport struct\n\nwith open('files/JUEGO.EXE', 'rb') as f:\n    data = f.read()\n\n# First call at file 0x259CB\nfile_offset = 0x259CB\ninsn = data[file_offset:file_offset+5]\nprint(f'Instruction bytes at file 0x{file_offset:05X}: {\" \".join(f\"{b:02X}\" for b in insn)}')\n\nif insn[0] == 0xE8:\n    rel = struct.unpack('&lt;i', insn[1:5])[0]\n    mem_addr = file_offset - 0x3200\n    target = mem_addr + 5 + rel\n    print(f'Call at mem 0x{mem_addr:05X}')\n    print(f'Relative offset: 0x{rel:X} ({rel})')\n    print(f'Target: mem 0x{target:05X} (file 0x{target+0x3200:05X})')\n    print()\n\n# Find all E8 calls in the palette fade snippets (0x259B1 to 0x25AB0)\nprint(\"All calls in palette fade region:\")\nfor i in range(0x259B1, 0x25AB0):\n    if data[i] == 0xE8:\n        rel = struct.unpack('&lt;i', data[i+1:i+5])[0]\n        mem_addr = i - 0x3200\n        target = mem_addr + 5 + rel\n        # Check the EAX value being passed (B8 XX XX 00 00 before call)\n        if i &gt;= 5 and data[i-5] == 0xB8:\n            eax_val = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[i-4:i])[0]\n            print(f'  CALL at mem 0x{mem_addr:05X} -&gt; 0x{target:05X}, EAX=0x{eax_val:X} ({eax_val})')\n        else:\n            print(f'  CALL at mem 0x{mem_addr:05X} -&gt; 0x{target:05X}')\n",
  "toolCallResult": null
}

{
  "invocationMessage": "Creating [](file:///Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/find_fc94_refs.py)",
  "pastTenseMessage": "Created [](file:///Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/find_fc94_refs.py)",
  "isConfirmed": {
    "type": 1
  },
  "content": "",
  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Find all references to step array at 0xFC94\"\"\"\nimport struct\n\narray_addr = 0xFC94  # Memory address of step array\narray_bytes = struct.pack('&lt;I', array_addr)\n\nwith open('files/JUEGO.EXE', 'rb') as f:\n    data = f.read()\n\nprint(f\"Searching for references to step array at 0x{array_addr:05X}...\")\nprint()\n\nidx = 0x3200  # Start of code section\ncount = 0\nwhile idx &lt; len(data):\n    pos = data.find(array_bytes, idx)\n    if pos == -1:\n        break\n    \n    mem_addr = pos - 0x3200\n    \n    # Get surrounding bytes for context\n    start = max(0, pos - 8)\n    end = min(len(data), pos + 12)\n    context = data[start:end]\n    \n    print(f\"Ref #{count+1} at file 0x{pos:05X} (mem 0x{mem_addr:05X}):\")\n    hex_str = ' '.join(f'{b:02X}' for b in context)\n    print(f\"  {hex_str}\")\n    \n    # Try to identify instruction type\n    # Check for indexed addressing like [reg*2 + 0xFC94]\n    if pos &gt;= 4:\n        prefix = data[pos-4:pos]\n        if prefix[0] == 0x66 and prefix[1] == 0x89 and prefix[2] == 0x04 and prefix[3] == 0x55:\n            print(\"  -&gt; MOV [EDX*2 + 0xFC94], AX (WRITE)\")\n        elif prefix[0] == 0x66 and prefix[1] == 0x8B and prefix[2] == 0x04 and prefix[3] == 0x55:\n            print(\"  -&gt; MOV AX, [EDX*2 + 0xFC94] (READ)\")\n        elif prefix[2] == 0x04 and prefix[3] == 0x55:\n            print(f\"  -&gt; Indexed by EDX*2, opcode prefix: {prefix[0]:02X} {prefix[1]:02X}\")\n        else:\n            print(f\"  -&gt; Prefix: {' '.join(f'{b:02X}' for b in prefix)}\")\n    \n    print()\n    count += 1\n    idx = pos + 1\n\nprint(f\"Total: {count} references\")\n",
  "toolCallResult": null
}
```

{
  "invocationMessage": "Creating [](file:///Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/find_fba0_refs.py)",
  "pastTenseMessage": "Created [](file:///Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/find_fba0_refs.py)",
  "isConfirmed": {
    "type": 1
  },
  "content": "",
  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Find all references to 0xFBA0 and 0xFBA2\"\"\"\nimport struct\n\naddresses = [0xFBA0, 0xFBA2, 0xFB9C]\n\nwith open('files/JUEGO.EXE', 'rb') as f:\n    data = f.read()\n\nfor target_addr in addresses:\n    print(f\"=== References to 0x{target_addr:05X} ===\")\n    target_bytes = struct.pack('&lt;I', target_addr)\n    \n    idx = 0x3200\n    count = 0\n    while idx &lt; len(data):\n        pos = data.find(target_bytes, idx)\n        if pos == -1:\n            break\n        \n        mem_addr = pos - 0x3200\n        start = max(0, pos - 8)\n        end = min(len(data), pos + 12)\n        context = data[start:end]\n        \n        print(f\"  Ref at file 0x{pos:05X} (mem 0x{mem_addr:05X}):\")\n        hex_str = ' '.join(f'{b:02X}' for b in context)\n        print(f\"    {hex_str}\")\n        \n        count += 1\n        idx = pos + 1\n    \n    print(f\"  Total: {count} refs\")\n    print()\n",
  "toolCallResult": null
}

{
  "invocationMessage": "Creating [](file:///Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/verify_palette_table.py)",
  "pastTenseMessage": "Created [](file:///Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/verify_palette_table.py)",
  "isConfirmed": {
    "type": 1
  },
  "content": "",
  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Verify the palette table structure at file 0x4C700 (mem 0x49500)\"\"\"\nimport struct\n\nwith open('files/JUEGO.EXE', 'rb') as f:\n    # File 0x4C700 = mem 0x49500\n    f.seek(0x4C700)\n    data = f.read(128)\n\nprint(\"=== Palette Fade Table at file 0x4C700 (mem 0x49500) ===\")\nprint()\n\n# Header (8 bytes)\nx, y, type_val, padding = struct.unpack('&lt;HHHH', data[0:8])\nprint(f\"Header: x={x}, y={y}, type={type_val}, pad={padding}\")\nprint()\n\n# 16 palette indices (16 bytes)\nindices = list(data[8:24])\nprint(f\"16 Palette indices: {indices}\")\nprint()\n\n# Source RGB (48 bytes at +0x18)\nprint(\"Source colors (16 × RGB, 6-bit):\")\nfor i in range(16):\n    r, g, b = data[0x18 + i*3], data[0x18 + i*3 + 1], data[0x18 + i*3 + 2]\n    idx = indices[i]\n    print(f\"  Index {idx:3d}: R={r:2d} G={g:2d} B={b:2d}   (8-bit: {r*4:3d},{g*4:3d},{b*4:3d})\")\nprint()\n\n# Target RGB (48 bytes at +0x48)\nprint(\"Target colors (16 × RGB, 6-bit):\")\nfor i in range(16):\n    r, g, b = data[0x48 + i*3], data[0x48 + i*3 + 1], data[0x48 + i*3 + 2]\n    idx = indices[i]\n    print(f\"  Index {idx:3d}: R={r:2d} G={g:2d} B={b:2d}   (8-bit: {r*4:3d},{g*4:3d},{b*4:3d})\")\nprint()\n\n# Compute delta for each color\nprint(\"Color deltas (target - source):\")\nfor i in range(16):\n    sr, sg, sb = data[0x18 + i*3], data[0x18 + i*3 + 1], data[0x18 + i*3 + 2]\n    tr, tg, tb = data[0x48 + i*3], data[0x48 + i*3 + 1], data[0x48 + i*3 + 2]\n    idx = indices[i]\n    dr, dg, db = tr - sr, tg - sg, tb - sb\n    print(f\"  Index {idx:3d}: ΔR={dr:+3d} ΔG={dg:+3d} ΔB={db:+3d}\")\n",
  "toolCallResult": null
}

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Find all references to palette table at 0x49500\"\"\"\nimport struct\n\n# The palette table is at memory 0x49500\npalette_table_addr = 0x49500\npalette_table_bytes = struct.pack('&lt;I', palette_table_addr)\n\nwith open('files/JUEGO.EXE', 'rb') as f:\n    data = f.read()\n\nprint(f\"Searching for references to palette table at 0x{palette_table_addr:05X}...\")\nprint()\n\n# Search for 4-byte address pattern\nidx = 0x3200\ncount = 0\nwhile idx &lt; len(data):\n    pos = data.find(palette_table_bytes, idx)\n    if pos == -1:\n        break\n    \n    mem_addr = pos - 0x3200\n    start = max(0, pos - 8)\n    end = min(len(data), pos + 12)\n    context = data[start:end]\n    \n    print(f\"Ref at file 0x{pos:05X} (mem 0x{mem_addr:05X}):\")\n    hex_str = ' '.join(f'{b:02X}' for b in context)\n    print(f\"  {hex_str}\")\n    \n    count += 1\n    idx = pos + 1\n\nprint(f\"\\nTotal: {count} refs\")\n\n# Also search for the header values (368, 148) which might be used\nprint(f\"\\n\\nSearching for potential related patterns...\")\n\n# Look for the palette indices list as a pattern\nindices_pattern = bytes([30, 37, 39, 41, 44, 62, 74, 79, 83, 89, 105, 120, 152, 179, 217, 238])\nidx = 0\nwhile True:\n    pos = data.find(indices_pattern, idx)\n    if pos == -1:\n        break\n    print(f\"Found palette indices at file 0x{pos:05X} (mem 0x{pos-0x3200:05X})\")\n    idx = pos + 1\n",

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Parse the item combination table entry for brick + window\"\"\"\nimport struct\n\nwith open('files/JUEGO.EXE', 'rb') as f:\n    # Read from file 0x4B320 where we found the entry\n    f.seek(0x4B320)\n    data = f.read(24)\n\nprint(\"Item combination table entries around brick+window:\")\nprint()\n\n# Each entry is 8 bytes: hotspot_id(2), item_id(2), func_ptr(4)\nfor i in range(0, 24, 8):\n    hotspot = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[i:i+2])[0]\n    item = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[i+2:i+4])[0]\n    func = struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[i+4:i+8])[0]\n    \n    marker = \" &lt;-- brick + window\" if hotspot == 294 and item == 4 else \"\"\n    print(f\"Entry at +{i:02X}: hotspot={hotspot:3d}, item={item:2d}, func=0x{func:05X}{marker}\")\n",
  "toolCallResult": null
}

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Find what code jumps/calls to 0x1284B\"\"\"\nimport struct\n\nwith open('files/JUEGO.EXE', 'rb') as f:\n    data = f.read()\n\ntarget = 0x1284B\n\nprint(f\"Searching for jumps/calls to 0x{target:05X}...\")\n\n# Search for E8 (call) and E9 (jmp) instructions\nfor i in range(0x3200, min(len(data)-5, 0x45000)):\n    if data[i] in (0xE8, 0xE9):\n        rel = struct.unpack('&lt;i', data[i+1:i+5])[0]\n        mem_addr = i - 0x3200\n        computed_target = mem_addr + 5 + rel\n        \n        if computed_target == target:\n            insn = \"CALL\" if data[i] == 0xE8 else \"JMP\"\n            print(f\"  {insn} at file 0x{i:05X} (mem 0x{mem_addr:05X}) -&gt; 0x{computed_target:05X}\")\n\n# Also check for indirect jumps through the table\nprint(f\"\\nAddress 0x{target:05X} appears in data at these locations:\")\ntarget_bytes = struct.pack('&lt;I', target)\nidx = 0x40000\nwhile idx &lt; len(data):\n    pos = data.find(target_bytes, idx)\n    if pos == -1:\n        break\n    print(f\"  File 0x{pos:05X} (mem 0x{pos-0x3200:05X})\")\n    idx = pos + 1\n",

}

  "content": "",
  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Disassemble the brick+window handler code manually\"\"\"\n\n# From the Ghidra disassembly, we can see the code around 0x1284B\n# Let me trace what happens when the dispatcher calls the function pointer\n\n# Looking at the raw bytes at 0x1284B:\n# 00 00 00 1F 00 - This looks like data, not code!\n# A1 C8 FA 00 00 - MOV EAX, [0xFAC8]\n\n# Wait - the first few bytes look wrong. Let me check if the table\n# has a different format\n\nimport struct\n\nwith open('files/JUEGO.EXE', 'rb') as f:\n    # Read the combo table entry again more carefully\n    f.seek(0x4B318)  # Start a bit before\n    data = f.read(32)\n\nprint(\"Item combo table entries (raw):\")\nfor i in range(0, 32, 8):\n    raw = data[i:i+8]\n    print(f\"  Offset +{i:02X}: {' '.join(f'{b:02X}' for b in raw)}\")\n    \n    hotspot = struct.unpack('&lt;H', raw[0:2])[0]\n    item = struct.unpack('&lt;H', raw[2:4])[0]\n    func = struct.unpack('&lt;I', raw[4:8])[0]\n    print(f\"    hotspot={hotspot}, item={item}, func=0x{func:05X}\")\n    print()\n\n# Now let's look at the actual code behavior\n# The dispatcher likely does: CALL [table + offset]\n# So the table contains function pointers, not direct offsets\n\n# Let's check what's at memory 0x48118 (the table base)\nprint(\"\\nTable base at mem 0x48118 (file 0x4B318):\")\nwith open('files/JUEGO.EXE', 'rb') as f:\n    f.seek(0x4B318)\n    for i in range(5):\n        entry = f.read(8)\n        hotspot = struct.unpack('&lt;H', entry[0:2])[0]\n        item = struct.unpack('&lt;H', entry[2:4])[0]\n        func = struct.unpack('&lt;I', entry[4:8])[0]\n        print(f\"  Entry {i}: hotspot={hotspot:3d}, item={item:2d}, func=0x{func:05X}\")\n",
  "toolCallResult": null
}

0x128AC) ===\")\n    print()\n    \n    # The bytes:\n    # 00 00 00 1F 00 - this looks like data but could be code\n    # A1 C8 FA 00 00 - MOV EAX, [0x4FAC8] = room_struct_ptr\n    # 31 D2          - XOR EDX, EDX\n    # 66 8B 90 BC 00 00 00 - MOV DX, [EAX+0xBC]\n    # ...\n    \n    print(\"Raw bytes:\")\n    for i in range(0, len(code), 16):\n        hex_str = ' '.join(f'{b:02X}' for b in code[i:i+16])\n        addr = 0x1284B + i\n        print(f'  {addr:05X}: {hex_str}')\n    \n    print()\n    print(\"Key addresses referenced:\")\n    \n    # Extract addresses from MOV EAX, [xxx] pattern (A1)\n    for i in range(len(code) - 4):\n        if code[i] == 0xA1:\n            addr = struct.unpack('&lt;I', code[i+1:i+5])[0]\n            mem_addr = 0x1284B + i\n            print(f'  0x{mem_addr:05X}: MOV EAX, [0x{addr:05X}]')\n    \n    # Extract immediate word values from 66 C7 80 xx xx xx xx yy yy\n    # MOV word ptr [EAX+offset], value\n    for i in range(len(code) - 8):\n        if code[i:i+2] == bytes([0x66, 0xC7]) and code[i+2] == 0x80:\n            offset = struct.unpack('&lt;I', code[i+3:i+7])[0]\n            value = struct.unpack('&lt;H', code[i+7:i+9])[0]\n            mem_addr = 0x1284B + i\n            print(f'  0x{mem_addr:05X}: MOV word ptr [EAX+0x{offset:X}], 0x{value:04X}')\n    \n    # Extract immediate byte values from C6 80 xx xx xx xx yy\n    # MOV byte ptr [EAX+offset], value\n    for i in range(len(code) - Table at data offset (mem 0x48118 + DATA_DELTA)\n        \n        print('=' * 70)\n        print('ITEM COMBINATION TABLE ANALYSIS')\n        print('=' * 70)\n        print()\n        print('Table location: Memory 0x48118, File 0x4B318')\n        print('Entry format: [hotspot:2][item:2][func_ptr:4]')\n        print()\n        print(f\"{'Entry':&lt;6} {'Hotspot':&lt;8} {'Item':&lt;5} {'MemAddr':&lt;10} {'FileAddr':&lt;10} {'FirstBytes':&lt;32}\")\n        print('-' * 70)\n        \n        for i in range(20):\n            entry = f.read(8)\n            hotspot, item, func_mem = struct.unpack('&lt;HHI', entry)\n            if hotspot == 0xFFFF:\n                print(f'{i:&lt;6} End marker (0xFFFF)')\n                break\n            \n            # Get file offset using code delta\n            func_file = func_mem + CODE_DELTA\n            \n            # Read the instruction at that address\n            pos = f.tell()\n            f.seek(func_file)\n            code = f.read(16)\n            f.seek(pos)\n            \n            code_hex = ' '.join(f'{b:02X}' for b in code)\n            print(f'{i:&lt;6} {hotspot:&lt;8} {item:&lt;5} 0x{func_mem:05X}   0x{func_file:05X}   {code_hex}')\n\ndef analyze_brick_handler():\n    \"\"\"Analyze what's at the brick handler address.\"\"\"\n    \n    print()\n    print('=' * 70)\n    print('BRICK HANDLER ANALYSIS (Entry 1: hotspot=294, item=4)')\n    print('=' * 70)\n    print()\n    \n    # The brick handler is at mem 0x1284B\n    # With CODE_DELTA: file = 0x1284B + 0x4200 = 0x16A4B\n    \n    with open('files/JUEGO.EXE', 'rb') as f:\n        f.seek(0x16A4B)\n        code = f.read(128)\n    \n    print(f'Handler at memory 0x1284B, file 0x16A4B')\n    print()\n    print('First 128 bytes:')\n    for i in range(0, len(code), 16):\n        addr = 0x1284B + i\n        hex_str = ' '.join(f'{b:02X}' for b in code[i:i+16])\n        print(f'  {addr:05X}: {hex_str}')\n    \n    # ## Summary

### The Combo Table Issue

The item combination table at memory address 0x48118 contains function pointers that **point to invalid addresses**. Specifically:
- Entry 1 (brick + window): `0x1284B` points 2 bytes into the middle of a `MOV BX, [0x4fb9e]` instruction inside `show_action_menu_popup`
- This is not a bug in our analysis - ALL the function pointers in this table appear to have this same issue

### Memory Offset Clarification

I discovered there are TWO different offset deltas for the EXE:
- **Code segment**: Memory + 0x4200 = File offset  
- **Data segment**: Memory + 0x3200 = File offset

The combo TABLE is in the data segment, but the function POINTERS in the table should reference code. Neither calculation produces valid function starts.

### Throwing Animation

The brick throwing animation is **NOT a special animation** in the `alfredSpecialAnims` array. The current ScummVM implementation doesn't have a dedicated throwing animation for Alfred - it just moves sprite 7 (the brick) upward toward the window.

Possible explanations:
1. The original game may not have a dedicated throw animation - just a standard Alfred pose while the brick sprite moves
2. The throw animation might use one of Alfred's existing action frames from ALFRED.3
3. The combo table may have been dynamically patched at runtime in the original DOS version

### Coordinates

The ScummVM implementation uses these coordinates:
- Brick starts at: `alfred.x - brickSprite.w/2`, `alfred.y - kAlfredFrameHeight`  
- Target: `windowHotspot.y + windowHotspot.h/2`
- Movement: 40 pixels upward per game tick

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Dump the item combo table from JUEGO.EXE\"\"\"\n\nimport struct\n\ndef main():\n    with open('files/JUEGO.EXE', 'rb') as f:\n        # Table at memory 0x48118, file offset = 0x48118 + 0x3200 = 0x4B318\n        f.seek(0x4B318)\n        \n        print('Combo Table entries:')\n        print('=' * 70)\n        print(f'Entry | Hotspot | Item | FuncPtr     | Notes')\n        print('-' * 70)\n        \n        for i in range(50):  # Read up to 50 entries\n            data = f.read(8)\n            if len(data) &lt; 8:\n                break\n            hotspot, item, func_ptr = struct.unpack('&lt;HHI', data)\n            if hotspot == 0xFFFF:\n                print(f'  {i:2d}  | 0xFFFF  |  --  |    --       | END MARKER')\n                break\n            \n            note = ''\n            if hotspot == 294 and item == 4:\n                note = '&lt;-- BRICK + WINDOW'\n            elif hotspot == 353 and item == 7:\n                note = '&lt;-- AMULET + STATUE'\n                \n            print(f'  {i:2d}  |  {hotspot:5d}  |  {item:2d}  | 0x{func_ptr:08X}  | {note}')\n\nif __name__ == '__main__':\n    main()\n",
  "toolCallResult": null
}

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Analyze the brick+window combo table dispatch\"\"\"\n\nimport struct\n\ndef main():\n    with open('files/JUEGO.EXE', 'rb') as f:\n        # Read combo table entry for brick+window\n        # Table at file offset 0x4B318\n        entry_offset = 0x4B318 + 1 * 8  # Entry 1\n        f.seek(entry_offset)\n        data = f.read(8)\n        hotspot, item, func_ptr = struct.unpack('&lt;HHI', data)\n        \n        print(f\"Brick+Window combo entry (index 1):\")\n        print(f\"  Hotspot: {hotspot} (0x{hotspot:04X})\")\n        print(f\"  Item: {item}\")\n        print(f\"  Function pointer: 0x{func_ptr:08X}\")\n        print()\n        \n        # The function pointer 0x0001284B is supposedly mid-instruction\n        # Let's check what bytes are there\n        \n        # Memory address 0x1284B -&gt; file offset 0x1284B + 0x4200 = 0x16A4B\n        code_file_offset = func_ptr + 0x4200\n        f.seek(code_file_offset)\n        code_bytes = f.read(32)\n        print(f\"Code bytes at 0x{func_ptr:X} (file offset 0x{code_file_offset:X}):\")\n        print(f\"  {' '.join(f'{b:02X}' for b in code_bytes)}\")\n        print()\n        \n        # Looking at the disassembly of show_action_menu_popup:\n        # 0x12849: MOV BX,word ptr [0x0004fb9e]  (66 8B 1D 9E FB 04 00)\n        # 0x12850: CMP CX,BX\n        \n        # So 0x1284B is 2 bytes into the MOV instruction\n        # The bytes there would be: 1D 9E FB 04 00 ...\n        \n        # Let's check the instruction at 0x12849\n        f.seek(0x12849 + 0x4200)\n        inst_bytes = f.read(7)\n        print(f\"Instruction at 0x12849:\")\n        print(f\"  {' '.join(f'{b:02X}' for b in inst_bytes)}\")\n        print(f\"  (MOV BX,word ptr [0x0004fb9e])\")\n        print()\n        \n        # This suggests the combo table entries for early items (0, 1, 2, etc.)\n        # have INVALID function pointers pointing mid-instruction\n        \n        # But wait - maybe the original game code was built differently,\n        # or these addresses mean something else\n        \n        # Let me check if maybe there's code at 0x1284B if we disassemble\n        # starting from there (maybe it's self-modifying or overlapping code?)\n        \n        print(\"Possible interpretation if 0x1284B is treated as instruction start:\")\n        # 1D = SBB EAX, imm32 (5 bytes)\n        # 9E FB 04 00 66 = operand for SBB EAX\n        print(f\"  1D 9E FB 04 00 = SBB EAX, 0x0004FB9E\")\n        print()\n        \n        # That doesn't make sense either as a function entry point\n        \n        # Let me check if the combo table dispatcher does something special\n        # with these early entries\n        \n        print(\"Checking if maybe these entries are never actually called...\")\n        print(\"Entry 0: hotspot 281, item 2 - func 0x127B2\")\n        print(\"Entry 1: hotspot 294, item 4 - func 0x1284B (brick+window)\")\n        print()\n        \n        # Let's look at what code exists just after show_action_menu_popup\n        # show_action_menu_popup: 0x124AD - 0x12917\n        # main_menu_handler: 0x12918 - 0x12C94\n        # Then there's code after 0x12C95\n        \n        # Maybe the early combo table entries were placeholders or\n        # the table format changed during development\n        \n        # Let me look for any code that looks like a brick throwing handler\n        # by searching for characteristic patterns\n        \n        print(\"Looking for potential brick handler patterns...\")\n        print(\"(searching for room 3 references, window animation, etc.)\")\n\nif __name__ == '__main__':\n    main()\n",
  "toolCallResult": null
}

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nVerify all combo table function pointers to find valid handlers.\nSome entries may have corrupted/invalid pointers pointing mid-instruction.\n\"\"\"\nimport struct\n\nEXE_PATH = \"files/JUEGO.EXE\"\nTABLE_FILE_OFFSET = 0x4B318  # Combo table at memory 0x48118 + DATA_DELTA 0x3200\nCODE_DELTA = 0x4200  # Memory address + CODE_DELTA = file offset\n\n# Known function boundaries from Ghidra\nKNOWN_FUNCTIONS = [\n    (0x124AD, 0x12917, \"show_action_menu_popup\"),\n    (0x12918, 0x12C94, \"main_menu_handler\"),\n    (0x12CC1, 0x12D1A, \"amulet_statue_handler_353_7\"),  # approximate\n    (0x12F06, 0x13000, \"unknown_handler\"),  # placeholder\n]\n\ndef get_function_containing(addr):\n    \"\"\"Find which function contains this address\"\"\"\n    for start, end, name in KNOWN_FUNCTIONS:\n        if start &lt;= addr &lt;= end:\n            return name, start, end\n    return None, None, None\n\ndef main():\n    with open(EXE_PATH, \"rb\") as f:\n        # Read combo table\n        entries = []\n        f.seek(TABLE_FILE_OFFSET)\n        entry_idx = 0\n        while True:\n            data = f.read(8)\n            if len(data) &lt; 8:\n                break\n            hotspot, item, func_ptr = struct.unpack(\"&lt;HHI\", data)\n            if hotspot == 0xFFFF:  # End marker\n                break\n            entries.append((entry_idx, hotspot, item, func_ptr))\n            entry_idx += 1\n        \n        print(f\"Found {len(entries)} combo table entries\")\n        print()\n        print(\"=\" * 80)\n        print(f\"{'Idx':&lt;4} {'Hotspot':&lt;8} {'Item':&lt;6} {'FuncPtr':&lt;10} {'Status':&lt;20} {'Function'}\")\n        print(\"=\" * 80)\n        \n        valid_count = 0\n        invalid_count = 0\n        \n        for idx, hotspot, item, func_ptr in entries:\n            func_name, func_start, func_end = get_function_containing(func_ptr)\n            \n            # Check if pointer is at function start (valid) or mid-function (invalid)\n            if func_name:\n                if func_ptr == func_start:\n                    status = \"VALID (at start)\"\n                    valid_count += 1\n                else:\n                    status = \"INVALID (mid-func)\"\n                    invalid_count += 1\n            else:\n                # Not in any known function - might still be valid\n                # Check if file offset is accessible and contains valid code\n                file_offset = func_ptr + CODE_DELTA\n                if file_offset &lt; 0 or file_offset &gt; 0x52000:\n                    status = \"INVALID (OOB)\"\n                    invalid_count += 1\n                else:\n                    status = \"UNKNOWN\"\n                    valid_count += 1  # Assume valid for unknown\n            \n            func_info = f\"{func_name or 'UNKNOWN'}\"\n            if func_name and func_ptr != func_start:\n                func_info += f\" (+0x{func_ptr - func_start:X})\"\n            \n            print(f\"{idx:&lt;4} {hotspot:&lt;8} {item:&lt;6} 0x{func_ptr:05X}   {status:&lt;20} {func_info}\")\n        \n        print(\"=\" * 80)\n        print(f\"Valid: {valid_count}, Invalid: {invalid_count}\")\n        \n        # Now let's look at the ACTUAL bytes at each function pointer\n        print()\n        print(\"=\" * 80)\n        print(\"First few bytes at each function pointer:\")\n        print(\"=\" * 80)\n        \n        for idx, hotspot, item, func_ptr in entries:\n            file_offset = func_ptr + CODE_DELTA\n            f.seek(file_offset)\n            bytes_at_ptr = f.read(8)\n            hex_bytes = \" \".join(f\"{b:02X}\" for b in bytes_at_ptr)\n            print(f\"Entry {idx}: 0x{func_ptr:05X} -&gt; {hex_bytes}\")\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n",

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nExamine ALFRED.3 to find character action animations.\nLooking for the 4-frame throwing animation.\n\"\"\"\nimport struct\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nALFRED3_PATH = \"files/ALFRED.3\"\n\n# Known animation set structure\nANIMATION_SETS = [\n    {\"frames\": 60, \"width\": 51, \"height\": 102, \"desc\": \"Walking cycle\"},\n    {\"frames\": 18, \"width\": 130, \"height\": 55, \"desc\": \"Wide animation\"},\n    {\"frames\": 25, \"width\": 51, \"height\": 100, \"desc\": \"Action animation\"},\n    {\"frames\": 10, \"width\": 51, \"height\": 100, \"desc\": \"Short action\"},\n    {\"frames\": 1, \"width\": 51, \"height\": 100, \"desc\": \"Static pose 1\"},\n    {\"frames\": 1, \"width\": 51, \"height\": 100, \"desc\": \"Static pose 2\"},\n    {\"frames\": 1, \"width\": 51, \"height\": 100, \"desc\": \"Static pose 3\"},\n    {\"frames\": 1, \"width\": 51, \"height\": 100, \"desc\": \"Static pose 4\"},\n    {\"frames\": 1, \"width\": 51, \"height\": 100, \"desc\": \"Static pose 5\"},\n    {\"frames\": 1, \"width\": 51, \"height\": 100, \"desc\": \"Static pose 6\"},\n    {\"frames\": 1, \"width\": 51, \"height\": 100, \"desc\": \"Static pose 7\"},\n    {\"frames\": 1, \"width\": 51, \"height\": 100, \"desc\": \"Static pose 8\"},\n    {\"frames\": 1, \"width\": 51, \"height\": 100, \"desc\": \"Static pose 9\"},\n]\n\ndef rle_decompress(data, max_output=1000000):\n    \"\"\"Simple RLE decompression for ALFRED format\"\"\"\n    output = bytearray()\n    i = 0\n    while i &lt; len(data) and len(output) &lt; max_output:\n        # Check for BUDA marker (end of data)\n        if data[i:i+4] == b'BUDA':\n            break\n        \n        byte = data[i]\n        if byte == 0xFF:\n            # Run length encoding\n            if i + 2 &lt; len(data):\n                count = data[i + 1]\n                value = data[i + 2]\n                output.extend([value] * count)\n                i += 3\n            else:\n                break\n        else:\n            # Literal byte\n            output.append(byte)\n            i += 1\n    \n    return bytes(output)\n\ndef main():\n    if not Path(ALFRED3_PATH).exists():\n        print(f\"File not found: {ALFRED3_PATH}\")\n        return\n    \n    with open(ALFRED3_PATH, \"rb\") as f:\n        data = f.read()\n    \n    print(f\"ALFRED.3 Analysis\")\n    print(\"=\" * 60)\n    print(f\"File size: {len(data):,} bytes\")\n    \n    # Find BUDA marker\n    buda_pos = data.find(b'BUDA')\n    if buda_pos != -1:\n        print(f\"BUDA marker at: 0x{buda_pos:X}\")\n    else:\n        print(\"No BUDA marker found\")\n    \n    print()\n    print(\"Animation Set Structure:\")\n    print(\"=\" * 60)\n    \n    offset = 0\n    total_expected = 0\n    \n    for i, anim in enumerate(ANIMATION_SETS):\n        size = anim[\"frames\"] * anim[\"width\"] * anim[\"height\"]\n        total_expected += size\n        print(f\"Set {i:2d}: {anim['frames']:2d} frames × {anim['width']}×{anim['height']} = \"\n              f\"{size:7,} bytes (offset: {offset:7,}) - {anim['desc']}\")\n        offset += size\n    \n    print()\n    print(f\"Total expected decompressed: {total_expected:,} bytes\")\n    \n    # Try to decompress and check\n    print()\n    print(\"Decompressing RLE data...\")\n    decompressed = rle_decompress(data)\n    print(f\"Decompressed size: {len(decompressed):,} bytes\")\n    \n    if len(decompressed) &gt;= total_expected:\n        print(\"✓ Decompressed data size matches expected!\")\n    else:\n        print(f\"! Decompressed is smaller than expected ({len(decompressed)} &lt; {total_expected})\")\n    \n    # The 4-frame throwing animation might be:\n    # 1. Frames within Set 2 (25 frames) or Set 3 (10 frames)\n    # 2. Static poses 1-4 (Sets 4-7)\n    \n    print()\n    print(\"Possible throwing animation locations:\")\n    print(\"=\" * 60)\n    \n    # Check if Sets 4-7 could be the 4 throwing frames\n    set4_offset = 60*51*102 + 18*130*55 + 25*51*100 + 10*51*100  # After sets 0-3\n    print(f\"Sets 4-7 start at offset: {set4_offset:,}\")\n    print(f\"Each static pose: 51×100 = 5,100 bytes\")\n    print(f\"4 static poses = 20,400 bytes\")\n    \n    # Or check within Set 2 (25 frames) - maybe frames 0-3 are throwing\n    set2_offset = 60*51*102 + 18*130*55\n    print(f\"\\nSet 2 (25 frames action) starts at: {set2_offset:,}\")\n    print(f\"First 4 frames of Set 2 = 4×51×100 = 20,400 bytes\")\n    \n    # Or within Set 3 (10 frames)\n    set3_offset = set2_offset + 25*51*100\n    print(f\"\\nSet 3 (10 frames short action) starts at: {set3_offset:,}\")\n    print(f\"First 4 frames of Set 3 = 4×51×100 = 20,400 bytes\")\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n",

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nSearch EXE for the brick throwing animation code.\nLooking for:\n1. References to item 4 (brick)\n2. References to hotspot 294 (0x126)\n3. Calls to play_fight_animation with different offsets\n\nThe known pattern for play_fight_animation is:\n  MOV EAX, &lt;offset&gt;           ; B8 xx xx xx xx\n  CALL play_fight_animation   ; E8 &lt;rel32 to 0x26420&gt;\n\"\"\"\nimport struct\n\nEXE_PATH = \"files/JUEGO.EXE\"\nCODE_DELTA = 0x4200\n\ndef main():\n    with open(EXE_PATH, \"rb\") as f:\n        data = f.read()\n    \n    print(\"=\" * 70)\n    print(\"SEARCH 1: Calls to play_fight_animation (0x26420)\")\n    print(\"=\" * 70)\n    \n    # play_fight_animation is at 0x26420\n    # CALL rel32 = E8 xx xx xx xx\n    # rel = target - (current + 5)\n    \n    calls_to_fight = []\n    for i in range(len(data) - 5):\n        if data[i] == 0xE8:  # CALL rel32\n            rel = struct.unpack(\"&lt;i\", data[i+1:i+5])[0]\n            mem_addr = i - CODE_DELTA\n            target = mem_addr + 5 + rel\n            if target == 0x26420:  # play_fight_animation\n                calls_to_fight.append((mem_addr, i))\n    \n    print(f\"Found {len(calls_to_fight)} calls to play_fight_animation:\")\n    for mem_addr, file_offset in calls_to_fight:\n        # Look backwards for MOV EAX, imm32 (B8 xx xx xx xx)\n        anim_offset = None\n        for back in range(1, 50):\n            pos = file_offset - back\n            if pos &gt;= 0 and data[pos] == 0xB8:\n                anim_offset = struct.unpack(\"&lt;I\", data[pos+1:pos+5])[0]\n                print(f\"  0x{mem_addr:05X}: animation offset = 0x{anim_offset:06X}\")\n                break\n        if anim_offset is None:\n            # Try MOV EAX, [addr] pattern (A1 xx xx xx xx)\n            for back in range(1, 50):\n                pos = file_offset - back\n                if pos &gt;= 0 and data[pos] == 0xA1:\n                    addr = struct.unpack(\"&lt;I\", data[pos+1:pos+5])[0]\n                    print(f\"  0x{mem_addr:05X}: animation from [0x{addr:05X}]\")\n                    break\n            else:\n                print(f\"  0x{mem_addr:05X}: (offset not found in preceding bytes)\")\n    \n    print()\n    print(\"=\" * 70)\n    print(\"SEARCH 2: References to hotspot 294 (0x126)\")\n    print(\"=\" * 70)\n    \n    # CMP word, 0x126 or MOV reg, 0x126, etc.\n    window_refs = []\n    val = 294\n    val_bytes = struct.pack(\"&lt;H\", val)\n    \n    for i in range(len(data) - 6):\n        # Check for 16-bit immediate 0x126\n        if data[i+1:i+3] == val_bytes or data[i+2:i+4] == val_bytes:\n            mem_addr = i - CODE_DELTA\n            if 0 &lt; mem_addr &lt; 0x40000:  # In code section\n                window_refs.append((mem_addr, data[i:i+8]))\n    \n    print(f\"Found {len(window_refs)} potential references to 0x126:\")\n    for mem_addr, context in window_refs[:30]:\n        print(f\"  0x{mem_addr:05X}: {context.hex()}\")\n    \n    print()\n    print(\"=\" * 70)\n    print(\"SEARCH 3: References to item 4 (brick)\")\n    print(\"=\" * 70)\n    \n    # Look for CMP with 4 near combo table handling code\n    # The combo table is checked around 0x191E9 (execute_complex_item_script_table)\n    \n    # Search for patterns checking item index\n    for i in range(len(data) -   "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nExamine the context around each play_fight_animation call to understand\nwhat animations they're playing.\n\"\"\"\nimport struct\n\nEXE_PATH = \"files/JUEGO.EXE\"\nCODE_DELTA = 0x4200\n\n# Animation offsets found that call play_fight_animation\nANIM_CALLS = [\n    (0x105AC, 0x2207FA, \"main_game_loop\"),  # Fight animation\n    (0x225B5, 0x2D5B98, \"unknown1\"),\n    (0x2315F, 0x1F7274, \"unknown2\"),\n    (0x23189, 0x204830, \"unknown3\"),\n    (0x23299, 0x17C03C, \"unknown4\"),\n    (0x23AFB, 0x186DBC, \"unknown5\"),\n    (0x2559B, 0x1AB1DC, \"unknown6\"),\n    (0x2583F, 0x2E5CF6, \"unknown7\"),\n    (0x25ADC, 0x182A56, \"unknown8\"),\n    (0x25B45, 0x1ADFD2, \"unknown9\"),\n    (0x25B9C, 0x1B02D4, \"unknown10\"),\n]\n\ndef main():\n    with open(EXE_PATH, \"rb\") as f:\n        data = f.read()\n    \n    print(\"Analyzing play_fight_animation calls\")\n    print(\"=\" * 70)\n    print()\n    \n    for call_addr, anim_offset, name in ANIM_CALLS:\n        print(f\"Call at 0x{call_addr:05X}, animation 0x{anim_offset:06X} ({name})\")\n        \n        # Get file offset\n        file_off = call_addr + CODE_DELTA\n        \n        # Look for context - what function is this in?\n        # Search backwards for PUSH 0x?? CALL (function prologue pattern)\n        func_start = None\n        for back in range(1, 1000):\n            pos = file_off - back\n            if pos &gt;= 0:\n                # Look for PUSH ebp at function start\n                if data[pos] == 0x55:  # PUSH EBP\n                    if pos + 1 &lt; len(data) and data[pos+1] in [0x89, 0x8B]:  # MOV EBP, ...\n                        func_start = pos - CODE_DELTA\n                        break\n                # Or PUSH imm32 (for alloc_memory style)\n                if data[pos] == 0x68 and pos + 5 &lt; len(data):\n                    # Check if next is CALL\n                    if data[pos+5] == 0xE8:\n                        func_start = pos - CODE_DELTA\n                        break\n        \n        if func_start:\n            print(f\"  Likely function start: 0x{func_start:05X}\")\n        \n        # Look at bytes around the call\n        start = max(0, file_off - 50)\n        end = min(len(data), file_off + 20)\n        \n        # Find what parameters are being passed before the animation call\n        print(f\"  Bytes before call:\")\n        \n        # Disassemble key instructions in the lead-up\n        pos = file_off - 50\n        while pos &lt; file_off:\n            if pos &lt; 0:\n                pos += 1\n                continue\n                \n            # PUSH instructions\n            if data[pos] == 0x68:  # PUSH imm32\n                imm = struct.unpack(\"&lt;I\", data[pos+1:pos+5])[0]\n                mem_addr = pos - CODE_DELTA\n                print(f\"    0x{mem_addr:05X}: PUSH 0x{imm:X}\")\n                pos += 5\n            elif data[pos] == 0x6A:  # PUSH imm8\n                imm = data[pos+1]\n                mem_addr = pos - CODE_DELTA\n                print(f\"    0x{mem_addr:05X}: PUSH 0x{imm:X}\")\n                pos += 2\n            elif data[pos] == 0xB8:  # MOV EAX, imm32\n                imm = struct.unpack(\"&lt;I\", data[pos+1:pos+5])[0]\n                mem_addr = pos - CODE_DELTA\n                if imm &gt; 0x10000:  # Likely animation offset\n                    print(f\"    0x{mem_addr:05X}: MOV EAX, 0x{imm:X} &lt;-- ANIMATION OFFSET\")\n                pos += 5\n            elif data[pos] == 0xBA:  # MOV EDX, imm32\n                imm = struct.unpack(\"&lt;I\", data[pos+1:pos+5])[0]\n                mem_addr = pos - CODE_DELTA\n                print(f\"    0x{mem_addr:05X}: MOV EDX, 0x{imm:X}\")\n                pos += 5\n            elif data[pos] == 0xBB:  # MOV EBX, imm32\n                imm = struct.unpack(\"&lt;I\", data[pos+1:pos+5])[0]\n                mem_addr = pos - CODE_DELTA\n                print(f\"    0x{mem_addr:05X}: MOV EBX, 0x{imm:X}\")\n                pos += 5\n            else:\n                pos += 1\n        \n        print()\n    \n    print()\n    print(\"=\" * 70)\n    print(\"Animation offset ranges in ALFRED.7:\")\n    print(\"-\" * 70)\n    \n    offsets = sorted([o for _, o, _ in ANIM_CALLS])\n    for off in offsets:\n        print(f\"  0x{off:06X}\")\n    \n    print()\n    print(\"The throwing animation (4 frames) should be around 0x108C2 (idle)\")\n    print(\"or in a similar range.   "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nDump and analyze the full combo table (item+hotspot combinations).\nFocus on finding any entries related to room 3 or brick/window.\n\"\"\"\nimport struct\n\nEXE_PATH = \"files/JUEGO.EXE\"\nDATA_DELTA = 0x3200\n\n# Combo table is at memory address 0x48118, file offset = 0x4B318\nCOMBO_TABLE_FILE_OFFSET = 0x4B318\n\n# Known hotspots\nHOTSPOTS = {\n    294: \"Window (room 3)\",\n    353: \"Statue\",\n}\n\n# Known items  \nITEMS = {\n    4: \"Brick\",\n    7: \"Amulet\",\n}\n\ndef main():\n    with open(EXE_PATH, \"rb\") as f:\n        data = f.read()\n    \n    print(\"Full Combo Table Analysis\")\n    print(\"=\" * 80)\n    print()\n    print(\"Format: [hotspot_id:2][item_id:2][func_ptr:4] = 8 bytes per entry\")\n    print()\n    \n    pos = COMBO_TABLE_FILE_OFFSET\n    entry = 0\n    \n    # Group by hotspot ID\n    entries_by_hotspot = {}\n    \n    while pos &lt; len(data) - 8:\n        hotspot_id = struct.unpack(\"&lt;H\", data[pos:pos+2])[0]\n        item_id = struct.unpack(\"&lt;H\", data[pos+2:pos+4])[0]\n        func_ptr = struct.unpack(\"&lt;I\", data[pos+4:pos+8])[0]\n        \n        if hotspot_id == 0xFFFF:\n            print(f\"Entry {entry}: END OF TABLE\")\n            break\n        \n        hotspot_name = HOTSPOTS.get(hotspot_id, \"\")\n        item_name = ITEMS.get(item_id, \"\")\n        \n        if hotspot_id not in entries_by_hotspot:\n            entries_by_hotspot[hotspot_id] = []\n        entries_by_hotspot[hotspot_id].append((entry, item_id, item_name, func_ptr))\n        \n        # Mark interesting entries\n        mark = \"\"\n        if hotspot_id == 294 or item_id == 4:\n            mark = \" &lt;-- BRICK/WINDOW!\"\n        elif hotspot_name or item_name:\n            mark = \" &lt;-- KNOWN\"\n        \n        print(f\"Entry {entry:3d}: hotspot={hotspot_id:4d} ({hotspot_name:20s}) item={item_id:3d} ({item_name:10s}) -&gt; 0x{func_ptr:05X}{mark}\")\n        \n        pos += 8\n        entry += 1\n    \n    print()\n    print(\"=\" * 80)\n    print(\"Entries grouped by hotspot (looking for room 3 hotspots):\")\n    print(\"-\" * 80)\n    \n    # Room 3 hotspot IDs are typically in a specific range\n    # Let's print hotspots that might be in room 3\n    for hotspot_id in sorted(entries_by_hotspot.keys()):\n        entries = entries_by_hotspot[hotspot_id]\n        if len(entries) &gt; 1 or hotspot_id == 294:\n            print(f\"\\nHotspot {hotspot_id}:\")\n            for entry_num, item_id, item_name, func_ptr in entries:\n                print(f\"  Entry {entry_num}: item {item_id} ({item_name}) -&gt; 0x{func_ptr:05X}\")\n    \n    print()\n    print(\"=\" * 80)\n    print(\"Searching for animation loading patterns in combo handler functions:\")\n    print(\"-\" * 80)\n    \n    # Look at each function pointer to see if any load animations\n    seen_funcs = set()\n    for hotspot_id, entries in entries_by_hotspot.items():\n        for entry_num, item_id, item_name, func_ptr in entries:\n            if func_ptr in seen_funcs:\n                continue\n            seen_funcs.add(func_ptr)\n            \n            # Get file offset\n            file_off = func_ptr + 0x4200  # CODE_DELTA\n            \n            if file_off &lt; 0 or file_off &gt;= len(data) - 200:\n                continue\n            \n            # Search for file_seek calls in the first 200 bytes\n            for i in range(200):\n                pos = file_off + i\n                if pos &gt;= len(data) - 5:\n                    break\n                if data[pos] == 0xE8:  # CALL\n                    rel = struct.unpack(\"&lt;i\", data[pos+1:pos+5])[0]\n                    target = (func_ptr + i + 5 + rel) &amp; 0xFFFFFFFF\n                    if target == 0x2A342:  # file_seek\n                        # Look backwards for offset\n                        for back in range(1, 30):\n                            check_pos = pos - back\n                            if check_pos &gt;= file_off and data[check_pos] == 0xB8:  # MOV EAX\n                                offset = struct.unpack(\"&lt;I\", data[check_pos+1:check_pos+5])[0]\n                                if 0x10000 &lt; offset &lt; 0x400000:\n                                    print(f\"  Func 0x{func_ptr:05X} (entry {entry_num}): loads anim at 0x{offset:06X}\")\n                                    break\n                        break\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n",

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nCheck if brick combo table entries are valid code entry points.\n\"\"\"\nimport struct\n\nEXE_PATH = \"files/JUEGO.EXE\"\nCODE_DELTA = 0x4200\n\n# Brick-related entries\nBRICK_ENTRIES = [\n    (1, 294, 4, 0x1284B, \"window (room 3)\"),\n    (2, 295, 4, 0x12AF7, \"hotspot 295\"),  \n    (10, 358, 4, 0x12EA1, \"hotspot 358\"),\n]\n\ndef main():\n    with open(EXE_PATH, \"rb\") as f:\n        data = f.read()\n    \n    print(\"Analyzing brick combo table entries\")\n    print(\"=\" * 70)\n    \n    for entry_num, hotspot, item, func_ptr, desc in BRICK_ENTRIES:\n        print(f\"\\nEntry {entry_num}: hotspot {hotspot} ({desc}) + brick -&gt; 0x{func_ptr:05X}\")\n        \n        file_off = func_ptr + CODE_DELTA\n        \n        # Show bytes at the address\n        print(f\"  File offset: 0x{file_off:X}\")\n        bytes_at = data[file_off:file_off+16]\n        print(f\"  Bytes: {bytes_at.hex()}\")\n        \n        # Check if starts with PUSH (0x68/0x6A) or common prologue\n        first_byte = bytes_at[0]\n        \n        if first_byte == 0x68:  # PUSH imm32\n            imm = struct.unpack(\"&lt;I\", bytes_at[1:5])[0]\n            print(f\"  Instruction: PUSH 0x{imm:X}\")\n            print(f\"  VALID: Function prologue (alloc_memory pattern)\")\n        elif first_byte == 0x55:  # PUSH EBP\n            print(f\"  Instruction: PUSH EBP\")\n            print(f\"  VALID: Standard function prologue\")\n        elif first_byte == 0x66:  # 16-bit prefix\n            print(f\"  Instruction: 16-bit prefix (0x66 ...)\")\n            # Check next byte\n            if bytes_at[1] == 0x8B:  # MOV r16, ...\n                print(f\"  This is a MOV instruction - NOT a valid function entry!\")\n                print(f\"  INVALID: Points mid-instruction or to non-entry code\")\n        elif first_byte == 0xC3:\n            print(f\"  Instruction: RET\")\n            print(f\"  INVALID: Points to return instruction\")\n        elif first_byte == 0xE8:  # CALL\n            rel = struct.unpack(\"&lt;i\", bytes_at[1:5])[0]\n            target = func_ptr + 5 + rel\n            print(f\"  Instruction: CALL 0x{target:05X}\")\n            print(f\"  Possibly valid - call as first instruction\")\n        elif first_byte == 0x83:  # CMP/ADD/etc r/m32, imm8\n            print(f\"  Instruction: 0x83 (CMP/ADD/SUB etc)\")\n            print(f\"  Might be jump target inside function\")\n        elif first_byte == 0xE9:  # JMP rel32\n            rel = struct.unpack(\"&lt;i\", bytes_at[1:5])[0]\n            target = func_ptr + 5 + rel\n            print(f\"  Instruction: JMP 0x{target:05X}\")\n            print(f\"  VALID: Trampoline jump\")\n        else:\n            print(f\"  First byte: 0x{first_byte:02X}\")\n            print(f\"  UNKNOWN: Need to analyze\")\n        \n        # Look for nearby function boundaries\n        print(f\"\\n  Searching for nearby function prologues...\")\n        for back in range(1, 100):\n            check_pos = file_off - back\n            if check_pos &gt;= 0:\n                if data[check_pos] == 0x68 and data[check_pos+5] == 0xE8:  # PUSH imm32; CALL\n                    func_start = check_pos - CODE_DELTA\n                    print(f\"  Found function start at 0x{func_start:05X} ({back} bytes before)\")\n                    print(f\"  Our pointer is 0x{func_ptr:05X} = entry + 0x{back:X}\")\n                    break\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n",

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nDisassemble around 0x12E9D to understand the brick handler.\n\"\"\"\nimport struct\nfrom capstone import *\n\nEXE_PATH = \"files/JUEGO.EXE\"\nCODE_DELTA = 0x4200\n\ndef main():\n    with open(EXE_PATH, \"rb\") as f:\n        data = f.read()\n    \n    # Try disassembling at 0x12E9D\n    mem_addr = 0x12E9D\n    file_off = mem_addr + CODE_DELTA\n    \n    code = data[file_off:file_off+200]\n    \n    md = Cs(CS_ARCH_X86, CS_MODE_32)\n    md.detail = True\n    \n    print(f\"Disassembly starting at 0x{mem_addr:05X}:\")\n    print(\"=\" * 70)\n    \n    for i in md.disasm(code, mem_addr):\n        # Mark the entry point\n        marker = \"\"\n        if i.address == 0x12EA1:\n            marker = \" &lt;-- ENTRY POINT (combo table pointer)\"\n        print(f\"0x{i.address:05X}: {i.mnemonic:8s} {i.op_str}{marker}\")\n        \n        # Stop after a RET or JMP far\n        if i.mnemonic == 'ret' or (i.mnemonic == 'jmp' and i.address &gt; 0x12EB0):\n            break\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n",

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nSearch for all hardcoded ALFRED.7 offsets in the code that are in a similar\nrange to the idle animation (0x108C2, 0x15958).\n\nThe throwing animation should be a small animation (4 frames) so it's likely\nin the same range.\n\"\"\"\nimport struct\n\nEXE_PATH = \"files/JUEGO.EXE\"\nCODE_DELTA = 0x4200\n\n# Known ALFRED.7 offsets for character animations\nKNOWN_OFFSETS = {\n    0x108C2: \"idle_comb_right\",\n    0x15958: \"idle_comb_left\",\n    0x2207FA: \"fight_animation\",\n}\n\ndef main():\n    with open(EXE_PATH, \"rb\") as f:\n        data = f.read()\n    \n    print(\"Searching for hardcoded ALFRED.7 offsets in small animation range (0x10000-0x200000)\")\n    print(\"=\" * 70)\n    \n    # Search for MOV EAX, imm32 where imm32 is in our target range\n    found_offsets = []\n    \n    for i in range(len(data) - 5):\n        if data[i] == 0xB8:  # MOV EAX, imm32\n            imm = struct.unpack(\"&lt;I\", data[i+1:i+5])[0]\n            if 0x10000 &lt;= imm &lt;= 0x200000:\n                mem_addr = i - CODE_DELTA\n                if 0 &lt; mem_addr &lt; 0x40000:  # In code section\n                    found_offsets.append((mem_addr, imm, \"MOV EAX\"))\n        \n        # Also check PUSH imm32\n        if data[i] == 0x68:  # PUSH imm32\n            imm = struct.unpack(\"&lt;I\", data[i+1:i+5])[0]\n            if 0x10000 &lt;= imm &lt;= 0x200000:\n                mem_addr = i - CODE_DELTA\n                if 0 &lt; mem_addr &lt; 0x40000:\n                    found_offsets.append((mem_addr, imm, \"PUSH\"))\n    \n    # Sort by offset value\n    found_offsets.sort(key=lambda x: x[1])\n    \n    print(f\"Found {len(found_offsets)} potential ALFRED.7 offsets:\")\n    print()\n    \n    # Group by similar offset values\n    current_group = []\n    last_offset = 0\n    \n    for mem_addr, offset, pattern in found_offsets:\n        known = KNOWN_OFFSETS.get(offset, \"\")\n        marker = \" &lt;-- KNOWN: \" + known if known else \"\"\n        \n        # Check if this is near the idle range (0x108C2 - 0x15958)\n        if 0x10000 &lt;= offset &lt;= 0x20000:\n            marker += \" [IDLE RANGE]\"\n        \n        print(f\"  0x{mem_addr:05X}: {pattern:8s} 0x{offset:06X}{marker}\")\n    \n    print()\n    print(\"=\" * 70)\n    print(\"Offsets close to idle animation range (0x10000 - 0x20000):\")\n    print(\"-\" * 70)\n    \n    idle_range = [(m, o, p) for m, o, p in found_offsets if 0x10000 &lt;= o &lt;= 0x20000]\n    for mem_addr, offset, pattern in idle_range:\n        known = KNOWN_OFFSETS.get(offset, \"UNKNOWN\")\n        print(f\"  0x{mem_addr:05X}: {pattern:8s} 0x{offset:06X} ({known})\")\n    \n    print()\n    print(\"=\" * 70)\n    print(\"Looking for unknown offsets that might be throwing animation:\")\n    print(\"-\" * 70)\n    \n    # The throwing animation would be similar size to idle but smaller\n    # Idle is at 0x108C2, so look for offsets near that\n    for mem_addr, offset, pattern in found_offsets:\n        if offset not in KNOWN_OFFSETS:\n            if 0x10000 &lt;= offset &lt;= 0x18000:\n                # Check what function this is in by searching for nearby CALL\n                file_off = mem_addr + CODE_DELTA\n                has_file_call = False\n                for delta in range(5, 50):\n                    pos = file_off + delta\n                    if pos &lt; len(data) - 5 and data[pos] == 0xE8:\n                        rel = struct.unpack(\"&lt;i\", data[pos+1:pos+5])[0]\n                        target = mem_addr + delta + 5 + rel\n                        if target == 0x2A342:  # file_seek\n                            has_file_call = True\n                            break\n                \n                if has_file_call:\n                    print(f\"  0x{mem_addr:05X}: {pattern:8s} 0x{offset:06X} -&gt; file_seek() called\")\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n",
