  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nExamine the code at 0x23A26 which loads offset 0x158F8 and calls file_seek.\nThis might be related to the throwing animation.\n\"\"\"\nimport struct\n\nEXE_PATH = \"files/JUEGO.EXE\"\nCODE_DELTA = 0x4200\n\ndef simple_disasm(data, start_mem, length=150):\n    \"\"\"Simple x86 disassembler for common patterns\"\"\"\n    pos = 0\n    result = []\n    \n    while pos &lt; length:\n        file_off = start_mem + CODE_DELTA + pos\n        if file_off &gt;= len(data):\n            break\n            \n        b = data[file_off]\n        \n        if b == 0xB8:  # MOV EAX, imm32\n            imm = struct.unpack(\"&lt;I\", data[file_off+1:file_off+5])[0]\n            result.append((start_mem + pos, f\"MOV EAX, 0x{imm:X}\"))\n            pos += 5\n        elif b == 0xBA:  # MOV EDX, imm32\n            imm = struct.unpack(\"&lt;I\", data[file_off+1:file_off+5])[0]\n            result.append((start_mem + pos, f\"MOV EDX, 0x{imm:X}\"))\n            pos += 5\n        elif b == 0xBB:  # MOV EBX, imm32\n            imm = struct.unpack(\"&lt;I\", data[file_off+1:file_off+5])[0]\n            result.append((start_mem + pos, f\"MOV EBX, 0x{imm:X}\"))\n            pos += 5\n        elif b == 0xB9:  # MOV ECX, imm32\n            imm = struct.unpack(\"&lt;I\", data[file_off+1:file_off+5])[0]\n            result.append((start_mem + pos, f\"MOV ECX, 0x{imm:X}\"))\n            pos += 5\n        elif b == 0xE8:  # CALL rel32\n            rel = struct.unpack(\"&lt;i\", data[file_off+1:file_off+5])[0]\n            target = start_mem + pos + 5 + rel\n            result.append((start_mem + pos, f\"CALL 0x{target:X}\"))\n            pos += 5\n        elif b == 0xE9:  # JMP rel32\n            rel = struct.unpack(\"&lt;i\", data[file_off+1:file_off+5])[0]\n            target = start_mem + pos + 5 + rel\n            result.append((start_mem + pos, f\"JMP 0x{target:X}\"))\n            pos += 5\n        elif b == 0x68:  # PUSH imm32\n            imm = struct.unpack(\"&lt;I\", data[file_off+1:file_off+5])[0]\n            result.append((start_mem + pos, f\"PUSH 0x{imm:X}\"))\n            pos += 5\n        elif b == 0x6A:  # PUSH imm8\n            imm = data[file_off+1]\n            result.append((start_mem + pos, f\"PUSH 0x{imm:X}\"))\n            pos += 2\n        elif b == 0xC3:  # RET\n            result.append((start_mem + pos, \"RET\"))\n            pos += 1\n            break\n        elif b == 0x55:  # PUSH EBP\n            result.append((start_mem + pos, \"PUSH EBP\"))\n            pos += 1\n        elif b == 0x31:  # XOR\n            result.append((start_mem + pos, f\"XOR ...\"))\n            pos += 2\n        elif b == 0x33:  # XOR\n            result.append((start_mem + pos, f\"XOR ...\"))\n            pos += 2\n        else:\n            result.append((start_mem + pos, f\"[0x{b:02X}]\"))\n            pos += 1\n    \n    return result\n\ndef main():\n    with open(EXE_PATH, \"rb\") as f:\n        data = f.read()\n    \n    # Examine 0x23A26 which loads 0x158F8\n    target_addr = 0x23A26\n    \n    print(f\"Examining code around 0x{target_addr:05X} (loads offset 0x158F8):\")\n    print(\"=\" * 70)\n    \n    # Search backwards for function start\n    file_off = target_addr + CODE_DELTA\n    func_start = None\n    for back in range(1, 500):\n        check_pos = file_off - back\n        if check_pos &gt;= 0:\n            if data[check_pos] == 0x68 and data[check_pos+5] == 0xE8:  # PUSH; CALL\n                func_start = check_pos - CODE_DELTA\n                break\n            if data[check_pos] == 0x55 and data[check_pos+1] == 0x89:  # PUSH EBP; MOV\n                func_start = check_pos - CODE_DELTA\n                break\n    \n    if func_start:\n        print(f\"Likely function start: 0x{func_start:05X}\")\n        start = func_start\n    else:\n        print(\"Could not find function start, showing from target-100\")\n        start = target_addr - 100\n    \n    print()\n    \n    # Get bytes\n    for addr, instr in simple_disasm(data, start, 200):\n        marker = \"\"\n        if addr == target_addr:\n            marker = \" &lt;-- LOADS 0x158F8\"\n        if addr == 0x23AFB:\n            marker = \" &lt;-- call to play_fight_animation\"\n        if \"0x2A342\" in instr:\n            marker = \" (file_seek)\"\n        if \"0x2A43E\" in instr:\n            marker = \" (file_read)\"\n        print(f\"0x{addr:05X}: {instr}{marker}\")\n    \n    print()\n    print(\"=\" * 70)\n    print(\"Analysis:\")\n    print(\"  0x158F8 is very close to idle_comb_left (0x15958)\")\n    print(\"  Difference: 0x15958 - 0x158F8 = 0x60 = 96 bytes\")\n    print(\"  This could be the throwing animation!\")\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n",

{
  "invocationMessage": "Creating [](file:///Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/extract_alfred3.py)",
  "pastTenseMessage": "Created [](file:///Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/extract_alfred3.py)",
  "isConfirmed": {
    "type": 1
  },
  "content": "",
  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nExtract ALFRED.3 animations and create sprite sheets to find the throwing animation.\n\nBased on documentation:\n- File is RLE compressed with BUDA marker\n- Contains multiple animation sets\n\nSet configurations:\nSet 0: 51x102, 60 frames - walking cycle\nSet 1: 130x55, 18 frames - wide animation (cutscene)\nSet 2: 51x100, 25 frames - action animation  \nSet 3: 51x100, 10 frames - short action\nSets 4-12: 51x100, 1 frame each - static poses\n\"\"\"\nimport struct\nimport os\nfrom PIL import Image\n\nALFRED3_PATH = \"files/ALFRED.3\"\nPALETTE_PATH = \"files/ALFRED.1\"  # Get palette from Room 0\nOUTPUT_DIR = \"output_alfred3\"\n\n# Animation set configurations\nANIM_SETS = [\n    {\"width\": 51, \"height\": 102, \"frames\": 60, \"name\": \"walking_cycle\"},\n    {\"width\": 130, \"height\": 55, \"frames\": 18, \"name\": \"cutscene\"},\n    {\"width\": 51, \"height\": 100, \"frames\": 25, \"name\": \"action_25frames\"},\n    {\"width\": 51, \"height\": 100, \"frames\": 10, \"name\": \"action_10frames\"},\n    {\"width\": 51, \"height\": 100, \"frames\": 1, \"name\": \"pose_4\"},\n    {\"width\": 51, \"height\": 100, \"frames\": 1, \"name\": \"pose_5\"},\n    {\"width\": 51, \"height\": 100, \"frames\": 1, \"name\": \"pose_6\"},\n    {\"width\": 51, \"height\": 100, \"frames\": 1, \"name\": \"pose_7\"},\n    {\"width\": 51, \"height\": 100, \"frames\": 1, \"name\": \"pose_8\"},\n    {\"width\": 51, \"height\": 100, \"frames\": 1, \"name\": \"pose_9\"},\n    {\"width\": 51, \"height\": 100, \"frames\": 1, \"name\": \"pose_10\"},\n    {\"width\": 51, \"height\": 100, \"frames\": 1, \"name\": \"pose_11\"},\n    {\"width\": 51, \"height\": 100, \"frames\": 1, \"name\": \"pose_12\"},\n]\n\ndef decompress_rle(data, start=0, max_output=None):\n    \"\"\"Decompress RLE data with BUDA signature support\"\"\"\n    output = bytearray()\n    pos = start\n    \n    # Check for BUDA signature\n    if data[pos:pos+4] == b'BUDA':\n        # Read uncompressed size (4 bytes after BUDA)\n        uncompressed_size = struct.unpack(\"&lt;I\", data[pos+4:pos+8])[0]\n        pos += 8\n        print(f\"BUDA header found, uncompressed size: {uncompressed_size}\")\n        if max_output is None:\n            max_output = uncompressed_size\n    \n    while pos &lt; len(data):\n        if max_output and len(output) &gt;= max_output:\n            break\n            \n        byte = data[pos]\n        pos += 1\n        \n        if byte &gt;= 0xC0:  # Run-length\n            count = byte - 0xC0\n            if count == 0:\n                count = 64  # 0xC0 means 64 repeats\n            if pos &gt;= len(data):\n                break\n            value = data[pos]\n            pos += 1\n            output.extend([value] * count)\n        else:  # Literal byte\n            output.append(byte)\n    \n    return bytes(output)\n\ndef load_palette(alfred1_path):\n    \"\"\"Load palette from ALFRED.1 Room 0\"\"\"\n    with open(alfred1_path, \"rb\") as f:\n        # Room 0 directory starts at offset 0\n        # Pair 11 is the palette (offset 11*8 = 88)\n        f.seek(0 + 88)\n        palette_offset = struct.unpack(\"&lt;I\", f.read(4))[0]\n        palette_size = struct.unpack(\"&lt;I\", f.read(4))[0]\n        \n        print(f\"Palette at offset 0x{palette_offset:X}, size {palette_size}\")\n        \n        f.seek(palette_offset)\n        raw_pal = f.read(768)  # 256 * 3\n        \n        # VGA palette is 6-bit, convert to 8-bit\n        palette = []\n        for i in range(256):\n            r = (raw_pal[i*3] &amp; 0x3F) * 4\n            g = (raw_pal[i*3+1] &amp; 0x3F) * 4\n            b = (raw_pal[i*3+2] &amp; 0x3F) * 4\n            palette.extend([r, g, b])\n        \n        return palette\n\ndef create_sprite_sheet(pixel_data, width, height, frames, palette, output_path):\n    \"\"\"Create a horizontal sprite sheet from raw pixel data\"\"\"\n    sheet_width = width * frames\n    sheet_height = height\n    \n    img = Image.new('P', (sheet_width, sheet_height))\n    img.putpalette(palette)\n    \n    for frame in range(frames):\n        frame_start = frame * width * height\n        frame_end = frame_start + width * height\n        \n        if frame_end &gt; len(pixel_data):\n            print(f\"Warning: Not enough data for frame {frame}\")\n            break\n        \n        frame_data = pixel_data[frame_start:frame_end]\n        \n        for y in range(height):\n            for x in range(width):\n                idx = y * width + x\n                if idx &lt; len(frame_data):\n                    pixel = frame_data[idx]\n                    img.putpixel((frame * width + x, y), pixel)\n    \n    img.save(output_path)\n    print(f\"Saved: {output_path}\")\n\ndef main():\n    os.makedirs(OUTPUT_DIR, exist_ok=True)\n    \n    # Load palette\n    print(\"Loading palette from ALFRED.1...\")\n    palette = load_palette(PALETTE_PATH)\n    \n    # Read ALFRED.3\n    print(f\"\\nReading {ALFRED3_PATH}...\")\n    with open(ALFRED3_PATH, \"rb\") as f:\n        data = f.read()\n    \n    print(f\"File size: {len(data)} bytes\")\n    \n    # Check header\n    if data[:4] == b'BUDA':\n        print(\"BUDA compression detected\")\n    \n    # Decompress\n    print(\"\\nDecompressing...\")\n    pixel_data = decompress_rle(data, 0)\n    print(f\"Decompressed size: {len(pixel_data)} bytes\")\n    \n    # Calculate expected total size\n    expected_total = sum(s[\"width\"] * s[\"height\"] * s[\"frames\"] for s in ANIM_SETS)\n    print(f\"Expected total: {expected_total} bytes\")\n    \n    # Extract each animation set\n    print(\"\\nExtracting animation sets...\")\n    offset = 0\n    \n    for i, anim in enumerate(ANIM_SETS):\n        w, h, frames = anim[\"width\"], anim[\"height\"], anim[\"frames\"]\n        name = anim[\"name\"]\n        \n        frame_size = w * h\n        total_size = frame_size * frames\n        \n        if offset + total_size &gt; len(pixel_data):\n            print(f\"Set {i} ({name}): Not enough data (need {total_size}, have {len(pixel_data) - offset})\")\n            # Still try to extract what we can\n            available_frames = (len(pixel_data) - offset) // frame_size\n            if available_frames &gt; 0:\n                frames = available_frames\n                total_size = frame_size * frames\n                print(f\"  Extracting {frames} frames instead\")\n            else:\n                break\n        \n        set_data = pixel_data[offset:offset + total_size]\n        output_path = os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, f\"set_{i:02d}_{name}_{w}x{h}_{frames}frames.png\")\n        \n        print(f\"Set {i} ({name}): {w}x{h}, {frames} frames, offset {offset}\")\n        create_sprite_sheet(set_data, w, h, frames, palette, output_path)\n        \n        offset += total_size\n    \n    print(f\"\\nRemaining data: {len(pixel_data) - offset} bytes\")\n    \n    # Save full decompressed data for analysis\n    raw_path = os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, \"alfred3_decompressed.raw\")\n    with open(raw_path, \"wb\") as f:\n        f.write(pixel_data)\n    print(f\"\\nSaved raw decompressed data to {raw_path}\")\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n",
  "toolCallResult": null
}

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nExplore the remaining 179,131 bytes of ALFRED.3 that weren't documented.\nTry to extract more animation frames.\n\"\"\"\nimport struct\nimport os\nfrom PIL import Image\n\nOUTPUT_DIR = \"output_alfred3\"\nRAW_PATH = os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, \"alfred3_decompressed.raw\")\nPALETTE_PATH = \"files/ALFRED.1\"\n\n# Known data ends at offset 665,220\nKNOWN_END = 665220\n\ndef load_palette(alfred1_path):\n    \"\"\"Load palette from ALFRED.1 Room 0\"\"\"\n    with open(alfred1_path, \"rb\") as f:\n        f.seek(0 + 88)  # Pair 11 offset\n        palette_offset = struct.unpack(\"&lt;I\", f.read(4))[0]\n        f.seek(palette_offset)\n        raw_pal = f.read(768)\n        \n        palette = []\n        for i in range(256):\n            r = (raw_pal[i*3] &amp; 0x3F) * 4\n            g = (raw_pal[i*3+1] &amp; 0x3F) * 4\n            b = (raw_pal[i*3+2] &amp; 0x3F) * 4\n            palette.extend([r, g, b])\n        \n        return palette\n\ndef create_image(pixel_data, width, height, palette, output_path):\n    \"\"\"Create image from raw pixel data\"\"\"\n    img = Image.new('P', (width, height))\n    img.putpalette(palette)\n    \n    for y in range(height):\n        for x in range(width):\n            idx = y * width + x\n            if idx &lt; len(pixel_data):\n                img.putpixel((x, y), pixel_data[idx])\n    \n    img.save(output_path)\n\ndef main():\n    # Load decompressed data\n    with open(RAW_PATH, \"rb\") as f:\n        data = f.read()\n    \n    print(f\"Total decompressed size: {len(data)} bytes\")\n    print(f\"Known animation data ends at: {KNOWN_END} bytes\")\n    print(f\"Remaining data: {len(data) - KNOWN_END} bytes\")\n    \n    # Load palette\n    palette = load_palette(PALETTE_PATH)\n    \n    remaining = data[KNOWN_END:]\n    print(f\"\\nRemaining data first 32 bytes: {remaining[:32].hex()}\")\n    \n    # Try different frame sizes that make sense for throwing animation\n    # The throwing animation is 4 frames, so we need to find what fits\n    \n    # Possible dimensions for a character action:\n    test_dims = [\n        (51, 100),  # Same as other action animations\n        (51, 102),  # Same as walking\n        (60, 100),  # Slightly wider\n        (40, 80),   # Smaller\n        (64, 100),  # Power of 2 width\n        (32, 64),   # Smaller power of 2\n    ]\n    \n    print(\"\\n\" + \"=\" * 70)\n    print(\"Trying different frame dimensions to find 4-frame animation:\")\n    print(\"=\" * 70)\n    \n    for w, h in test_dims:\n        frame_size = w * h\n        possible_frames = len(remaining) // frame_size\n        \n        if possible_frames &gt;= 4:\n            print(f\"\\n{w}x{h} = {frame_size} bytes/frame, could have {possible_frames} frames\")\n            \n            # Extract first 4 frames\n            for num_frames in [4, 5, 6, 8, 10]:\n                if num_frames &lt;= possible_frames:\n                    total_size = frame_size * num_frames\n                    \n                    # Create sprite sheet\n                    sheet_width = w * num_frames\n                    img = Image.new('P', (sheet_width, h))\n                    img.putpalette(palette)\n                    \n                    for frame in range(num_frames):\n                        frame_start = frame * frame_size\n                        frame_data = remaining[frame_start:frame_start + frame_size]\n                        \n                        for y in range(h):\n                            for x in range(w):\n                                idx = y * w + x\n                                if idx &lt; len(frame_data):\n                                    img.putpixel((frame * w + x, y), frame_data[idx])\n                    \n                    output_path = os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, f\"extra_{w}x{h}_{num_frames}frames.png\")\n                    img.save(output_path)\n                    print(f\"  Saved: {output_path}\")\n    \n    # Also try to see if there's more structured data\n    # Look for patterns in the remaining bytes\n    print(\"\\n\" + \"=\" * 70)\n    print(\"Analyzing remaining data structure:\")\n    print(\"=\" * 70)\n    \n    # Check for repeated patterns that might indicate frame boundaries\n    chunk_size = 5100  # 51x100 = 5100 bytes\n    chunks = len(remaining) // chunk_size\n    print(f\"\\nIf 51x100 frames: could be {chunks} frames + {len(remaining) % chunk_size} extra bytes\")\n    \n    # Create a big image showing all remaining data as 51x100 frames\n    if chunks &gt; 0:\n        img = Image.new('P', (51 * min(chunks, 35), 100))  # Max 35 frames wide\n        img.putpalette(palette)\n        \n        for frame in range(min(chunks, 35)):\n            frame_start = frame * chunk_size\n            frame_data = remaining[frame_start:frame_start + chunk_size]\n            \n            for y in range(100):\n                for x in range(51):\n                    idx = y * 51 + x\n                    if idx &lt; len(frame_data):\n                        img.putpixel((frame * 51 + x, y), frame_data[idx])\n        \n        output_path = os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, f\"extra_all_51x100_{min(chunks, 35)}frames.png\")\n        img.save(output_path)\n        print(f\"\\nSaved all frames view: {output_path}\")\n    \n    # Look for the 4-frame throwing specifically\n    # It should be right arm lifting motion - 4 distinct poses\n    print(\"\\n\" + \"=\" * 70)\n    print(\"If throwing animation is near the beginning of extra data:\")\n    print(\"=\" * 70)\n    \n    # The first 4 frames at 51x100\n    if len(remaining) &gt;= 4 * 5100:\n        img = Image.new('P', (51 * 4, 100))\n        img.putpalette(palette)\n        \n        for frame in range(4):\n            frame_start = frame * 5100\n            frame_data = remaining[frame_start:frame_start + 5100]\n            \n            for y in range(100):\n                for x in range(51):\n                    idx = y * 51 + x\n                    if idx &lt; len(frame_data):\n                        img.putpixel((frame * 51 + x, y), frame_data[idx])\n        \n        output_path = os.path.join(OUTPUT_DIR, \"extra_first4_51x100.png\")\n        img.save(output_path)\n        print(f\"Saved first 4 frames: {output_path}\")\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n",

DOSBox-X debugger is accessed differently than the original DOSBox debugger. Let me provide accurate instructions.Good to know - the throwing animation is not in ALFRED.3. Let's trace it with DOSBox-X debugger.

## DOSBox-X Debugger Instructions

### 1. Enter Debug Mode

**Option A - Start in debug mode:**
```bash
dosbox-x -debug
```

**Option B - Enter debugger while running:**
- Press **Alt+Pause** (or **Alt+Break**) while the game is running

### 2. Debugger Interface

Once in the debugger, you'll see:
- **Top left**: Register view (EAX, EBX, etc.)
- **Top right**: Data view (memory dump)
- **Middle**: Disassembly view
- **Bottom**: Command input line

### 3. Set Breakpoints

The combo table dispatch is at memory address `0x191E9`. For a DOS EXE, we need the segment:offset. In this game:

```
BP CS:91E9
```

Or try the full linear address if that doesn't work:
```
BP 191E9
```

**Alternative breakpoints to try:**

```
; Combo table lookup loop
BP CS:9287

; file_seek function (catches any animation loading)
BP CS:1A342
```

### 4. Run the Game

```
G
```
(or press **F5** to continue execution)

### 5. Navigate to Brick + Window

1. Load your save or navigate to **Room 3** (the room with the window)
2. Pick up the **brick** (item 4)
3. **Use brick on window** (hotspot 294)

### 6. When Breakpoint Hits

The debugger will stop. Examine:

```
; View registers
R

; View memory at combo table (0x48118)
D DS:8118

; Step one instruction
T

; Step over calls (execute call but don't step into)
P

; Continue to next breakpoint
G
```

### 7. Key Commands Reference

| Command | Action |
|---------|--------|
| `G` | Go/Continue |
| `T` | Trace (step into) |
| `P` | Proceed (step over) |
| `BP seg:off` | Set breakpoint |
| `BPList` | List breakpoints |
| `BPDEL #` | Delete breakpoint |
| `D seg:off` | Dump memory |
| `R` | Show registers |
| `U seg:off` | Unassemble at address |
| `Q` or **F5** | Exit debugger / continue |

### 8. What to Look For

When the brick+window action triggers:

1. **Check EAX** after the combo table lookup - it should contain the entry index
2. **Check the function pointer** at `DS:8118 + (entry * 8) + 4` - this is where it jumps
3. **Trace into the handler** to see what animation offset it loads

The handler should eventually call `file_seek` with an ALFRED.7 offset. Look for:
```
MOV EAX, <some_offset>    ; Animation data offset
CALL file_seek            ; Seek to it
```

### 9. Finding the Code Segment

If breakpoints aren't hitting, you may need to find the correct segment. After the game loads:

```
; Search for the combo table signature (hotspot 294 = 0x126, item 4 = 0x04)
S DS:0 FFFF 26 01 04 00
```

This searches for bytes `26 01 04 00` (294, 4 in little-endian).

Information about the DOSBox-X Debugger

Debugger interface
------------------

In builds where it is enabled, DOSBox-X supports breaking into the debugger
interface, which is shown on the console.

A mapper shortcut is provided to break into the debugger on demand. Normally
this shortcut is set to Alt+Pause (Mac: Alt+F12).

In Windows, DOSBox-X can create a console and show the debugger interface
on it.

On other systems including Linux and Mac OS X, DOSBox-X must be started
from a terminal in order to enable the debugger.

The debugger interface should scale and respond to resizing of the
terminal window.

WARNING: Fitting to the window was added in DOSBox-X. The debugger
         interface in DOSBox SVN requires a minimum terminal window
         size to function, and may segfault if the terminal is too
         small.

The debugger interface is written against the "ncurses" library.

The window regions of the debugger interface are:
 - Register Overview
 - Data view
 - Code Overview
 - Variable (not shown by default)
 - Output

The register window will show at all times the contents of the CPU
registers and segment registers as well as other important CPU
state.

Data view allows viewing the contents of memory while debugging.
The location shown is controlled by a segment:offset pair.

In DOSBox-X, the Data view also permits viewing data as a linear
(pageable) offset and as a physical memory view (outside the
CPU's paging control).

The code overview/disassembly window shows the contents of a
memory location as disassembled x86 instructions. Normally, this
is set to the instruction pointer, but it can be set anywhere.
Decoding is based on the CPU mode.

The variable list is used when the debugger is given variables
to debug by.

The output window allows you to scroll through the last 1000
or so log messages written from within the codebase by LOG()
or LOG_MSG(). If the window is scrolled to the bottom, new
messages will appear by default.

The lowest row of the terminal is reserved for a line where
the user can enter debugger commands. An underscore shows
where the cursor is positioned.

The code and data views have been fixed in DOSBox-X to indicate
when data is not available to view for a specific segment:offset
or linear address.

If the CPU is in protected mode, and the segment portion refers
to a segment that does not exist, or the offset extends past
the limit of that segment, the code or data view will show
'na' instead of a byte value.

If 80386 paging is enabled, and the segment:offset or linear
address refers to a page that is not present, then the data
view will show 'pf' to indicate this.

  na = segment does not exist, or offset exceeds segment limit

  pf = segment:offset or linear address is paged out or
       not present according to page tables.

Debugging a program and breaking on start
-----------------------------------------

DOSBox-X includes a built-in command to launch a program and
break at the entry point.

DEBUGBOX [command] [options]

You can also type DEBUGBOX without a parameter to start the
debugger.

Debugger keyboard shortcuts
---------------------------

Tab/Shift+Tab       Switch to the next/previous window
F3/F6               Previous command in history
F4/F7               Next command in history
F5                  Resume emulation
F8                  Toggle printable characters display in data view
F9                  Set/clear breakpoint
F10                 Single step (over)
F11                 Single step (into)
Up arrow            Scroll up one line (if applicable)
Down arrow          Scroll down one line (if applicable)
Left arrow          Move cursor left in command line
Right arrow         Move cursor right in command line
Page Up/Fn+Up       Scroll up by window height (if applicable)
Page Down/Fn+Down   Scroll down by window height (if applicable)
Home/Fn+Left        Scroll to top (in Output window)
End/Fn+Right        Scroll to bottom (in Output window)
Insert              Toggle insert/overwrite mode in command line
Alt+D               Set data view to DS:SI
Alt+E               Set data view to ES:DI
Alt+X               Set data view to DS:DX
Alt+B               Set data view to ES:BX
Alt+S               Set data view to SS:SP

Debugger commands
-----------------

MOVEWINDN                                   Move current window down
MOVEWINDU                                   Move current window up
SHOWWIN <winname>                           Show window (by name)
HIDEWIN <winname>                           Hide window (by name)
MEMDUMP <seg> <off> <bytecount>             Dump memory to file (MEMDUMP.TXT)
MEMDUMPBIN <seg> <off> <bytecount>          Dump memory to file (MEMDUMP.BIN)
IV <seg> <off> <name>                       Insert variable
SV <name>                                   Save variables to <name>
LV <name>                                   Load variables from <name>
SR <reg> <value>                            Set register <reg> value to <value>
SM <seg> <off> [bytes in hex]               Set memory at <seg>:<off> to byte values given
BP <seg> <off>                              Add breakpoint (real mode)
BPM <seg> <off>                             Add breakpoint (protected mode)
BPLM <offset>                               Add breakpoint (linear/virtual address)
BPINT <intnum>                              Add breakpoint on interrupt
BPINT <intnum> <value>                      Add breakpoint on interrupt and AH=<value>
BPLIST                                      List breakpoints
BPDEL <breakpoint number>                   Delete breakpoint
RUN                                         Resume emulation
RUNWATCH                                    Resume emulation, but show state while running
A20                                         Show A20 gate state
A20 ON                                      Turn on A20 gate
A20 OFF                                     Turn off A20 gate
PIC                                         Show interrupt controller state
PIC MASKIRQ <irq>                           Mask IRQ at interrupt controller
PIC UNMASKIRQ <irq>                         Unmask IRQ at interrupt controller
PIC ACKIRQ <irq>                            Acknowledge IRQ at interrupt controller
PIC LOWERIRQ <irq>                          Manually lower interrupt signal
PIC RAISEIRQ <irq>                          Manually raise interrupt signal
C <seg> <off>                               Set code view to address
D <seg> <off>                               Set data view to address (segment:offset)
DV <offset>                                 Set data view to address (linear/virtual address)
DP <offset>                                 Set data view to address (physical)
LOG <hexadecimal count>                     Log CPU state, for the specified number of instructions, to LOGCPU.TXT
LOGS <hexadecimal count>                    Log CPU state, short log, to LOGCPU.TXT
LOGL <hexadecimal count>                    Log CPU state, long log, to LOGCPU.TXT
INTT <intnum>                               Trace interrupt
INT <intnum>                                Start interrupt
CALLBACKS                                   Show callbacks of interrupts.
SELINFO <n>                                 Show selector information
DOS MCBS                                    Dump DOS kernel MCB chain (conventional memory allocation chain)
DOS KERN                                    Dump DOS kernel memory allocation list
DOS XMS                                     Dump XMS (extended memory) allocation list
DOS EMS                                     Dump EMS (expanded memory) allocation list
BIOS MEM                                    Dump BIOS allocation and layout list
GDT                                         Dump GDT (global descriptor table)
LDT                                         Dump LDT (local descriptor table)
IDT                                         Dump IDT (interrupt descriptor table)
PAGING                                      Dump page table information
CPU                                         Dump additional CPU information
VGA cmd                                     VGA related debugging commands.
PC98 cmd                                    PC98 related debugging commands.
EMU MEM/MACHINE                             Show emulator memory or machine info.
INTVEC <file>                               Dump interrupt vector table to <file>
INTHAND <intnum>                            Set code view to start of interrupt handler
EXTEND                                      Toggle additional information
TIMERIRQ                                    Start timer IRQ
TIME <time>                                 Display or change the internal time
DATE <date>                                 Display or change the internal date
HEAVYLOG                                    Toggle heavy CPU logging
ZEROPROTECT                                 Toggle zero protection
HELP                                        Show some debugger commands for reference

## Corrected DOSBox-X Debugger Instructions

### 1. Start the game and enter debugger
```bash
dosbox-x
```
Then launch the game, and press **Alt+F12** (Mac) to break into debugger.

### 2. Find the code segment

First we need to find where JUEGO.EXE loaded. When in the debugger:

```
CPU
```

This shows CPU info including CS (code segment). Note the CS value.

### 3. Calculate and set breakpoint

The combo table dispatch function is at offset **0x191E9** in the executable. For DOS EXE, code typically starts around offset 0x10000 in the file, so:

**Try this address calculation:**
- Linear address: 0x191E9
- Typical DOS load: subtract 0x10000 (header) = 0x91E9

If CS shows as something like `01ED` or `1000`, try:

```
BP <CS_value> 91E9
```

Example if CS=01ED:
```
BP 01ED 91E9
```

**Or use linear breakpoint:**
```
BPLM 191E9
```

### 4. Alternative: Break on file operations

Since we want to catch animation loading, break on file_seek:

```
BPLM 2A342
```

This is the file_seek function - ANY animation load will hit this.

### 5. Continue and trigger

```
RUN
```

Then use brick on window in Room 3.

### 6. When it breaks

If it breaks at file_seek:
```
SR
```

Look at **EAX** or **EDX** - one contains the file offset being seeked to. This is your animation offset.

### 7. If still nothing happens

Try the interrupt breakpoint approach:
```
BPINT 21
RUN
```

This breaks on every DOS interrupt. It will break a LOT, but you can keep hitting F5 (RUN) until you trigger the brick+window action, then step through to see what happens.

### 8. Nuclear option - Step through manually

1. Enter debugger (Alt+F12)
2. Navigate to room 3 in game
3. Get brick in inventory
4. Click on brick, then **immediately press Alt+F12**
5. Now **repeatedly press F11** (step into) while watching the disassembly

This will be slow but you'll see every instruction as the action executes.

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Analyze LOGCPU.TXT to find unique addresses and patterns.\"\"\"\nimport re\nimport sys\n\nlog_path = '/Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/LOGCPU.TXT'\n\naddrs = {}\nwith open(log_path, 'r') as f:\n    for line in f:\n        # Match address at start: \"0160:001F2B86\"\n        m = re.match(r'([0-9A-Fa-f]+):([0-9A-Fa-f]+)', line)\n        if m:\n            seg = m.group(1)\n            off = m.group(2)\n            full = f\"{seg}:{off}\"\n            if full not in addrs:\n                addrs[full] = {'count': 0, 'example': line.strip()[:80]}\n            addrs[full]['count'] += 1\n\nprint(f\"Total unique addresses: {len(addrs)}\")\nprint(\"\\nAll addresses (sorted by offset):\")\nfor addr in sorted(addrs.keys(), key=lambda x: int(x.split(':')[1], 16)):\n    info = addrs[addr]\n    print(f\"  {addr}: {info['count']} times\")\n\nprint(\"\\n\\nMost frequent addresses:\")\nfor addr in sorted(addrs.keys(), key=lambda x: -addrs[x]['count'])[:10]:\n    info = addrs[addr]\n    print(f\"  {addr}: {info['count']} times\")\n    print(f\"    Example: {info['example'][:100]}\")\n",
  "toolCallResult": null
}

  "invocationMessage": "Creating [](file:///Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/calculate_base_offset.py)",
  "pastTenseMessage": "Created [](file:///Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/calculate_base_offset.py)",
  "isConfirmed": {
    "type": 1
  },
  "content": "",
  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nCalculate the base offset between Ghidra addresses and runtime addresses.\n\nFrom the log, we see runtime addresses like:\n  0160:001DD000  add  esp,0004\n  0160:001EB274  add  esp,0004\n  0160:001F2BB0  mov  edx,eax\n\nWe need to find patterns in the log that match known Ghidra code.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport re\n\n# Known Ghidra function starts\nghidra_funcs = {\n    'execute_complex_item_script_table': 0x191E9,\n    'play_fight_animation': 0x26420,\n    'file_seek': 0x2A342,\n    'main_game_loop': 0x10442,  # guessed from disassembly\n}\n\n# Runtime addresses from log\nruntime_addrs = [\n    0x1F2B86,  # mov  cl,[esi+000D]\n    0x1F2BB0,  # mov  edx,eax\n    0x1EB274,  # add  esp,0004\n    0x1DD000,  # add  esp,0004\n    0x1D615C,  # from unique addresses\n]\n\n# Try different base offsets\nprint(\"Trying different base offsets...\")\nfor base in [0x1C0000, 0x1CC000, 0x1D0000, 0x1E0000]:\n    print(f\"\\nBase offset: 0x{base:05X}\")\n    for name, ghidra in ghidra_funcs.items():\n        runtime = ghidra + base\n        print(f\"  {name}: Ghidra 0x{ghidra:05X} -&gt; Runtime 0x{runtime:06X}\")\n\n# Let's look at specific runtime addresses\nprint(\"\\n\\nRuntime addresses mapped back with different bases:\")\nfor base in [0x1C0000, 0x1CC000, 0x1D0000, 0x1E0000]:\n    print(f\"\\nBase 0x{base:05X}:\")\n    for runtime in runtime_addrs:\n        ghidra = runtime - base\n        if 0x10000 &lt;= ghidra &lt;= 0x50000:\n            print(f\"  Runtime 0x{runtime:06X} -&gt; Ghidra 0x{ghidra:05X}\")\n        else:\n            print(f\"  Runtime 0x{runtime:06X} -&gt; Out of range (0x{ghidra:05X})\")\n",
  "toolCallResult": null
}
```

  "pastTenseMessage": "Created [](file:///Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/find_base_offset.py)",
  "isConfirmed": {

  "content": "",
  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nFind the base offset by searching for specific instruction patterns.\n\nThe log shows:\n  0160:001F2BB0  mov  edx,eax\n\nLet me find where \"mov edx,eax\" exists in Ghidra and calculate the offset.\n\"mov edx,eax\" = 89 C2 (or 8B D0)\n\"\"\"\n\n# Known instruction at runtime 0x1F2BB0: mov edx,eax\n# Let's check what the opcode for \"mov edx,eax\" is:\n# 89 C2 = MOV r/m32, r32 (mov edx, eax where reg is source)\n# 8B D0 = MOV r32, r/m32 (mov edx, eax where reg is dest)\n\nimport struct\n\n# Read JUEGO.EXE\nwith open('files/JUEGO.EXE', 'rb') as f:\n    exe = f.read()\n\n# Search for MOV EDX,EAX (8B D0 or 89 C2)\npatterns = [\n    (b'\\x8B\\xD0', 'MOV EDX,EAX (8B D0)'),\n    (b'\\x89\\xC2', 'MOV EDX,EAX (89 C2)'),\n]\n\nprint(\"Searching for MOV EDX,EAX in JUEGO.EXE...\")\nfor pattern, desc in patterns:\n    count = 0\n    idx = 0\n    while True:\n        pos = exe.find(pattern, idx)\n        if pos == -1:\n            break\n        count += 1\n        # File offset to Ghidra address (subtract 0x3200 for typical DOS4GW)\n        ghidra_addr = pos - 0x3200\n        if count &lt;= 10:\n            print(f\"  Found at file 0x{pos:05X}, Ghidra ~0x{ghidra_addr:05X}: {desc}\")\n        idx = pos + 1\n    print(f\"  Total: {count} occurrences\")\n\n# Now let's compute what the base would be for runtime 0x1F2BB0\n# If this instruction is at Ghidra address X, then base = 0x1F2BB0 - X\nprint(\"\\n\\nPossible base offsets for runtime 0x1F2BB0:\")\ntest_ghidra = [0x26BB0, 0x12BB0, 0x1F2BB0 - 0x1CC000, 0x1F2BB0 - 0x1C0000]\nfor g in test_ghidra:\n    if 0 &lt; g &lt; 0x50000:\n        base = 0x1F2BB0 - g\n        print(f\"  If Ghidra=0x{g:05X}, Base=0x{base:05X}\")\n",
  "toolCallResult": null
}
```

{
  "invocationMessage": "Creating [](file:///Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/trace_anim_calls.py)",
  "pastTenseMessage": "Created [](file:///Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/trace_anim_calls.py)",
  "isConfirmed": {
    "type": 1
  },
  "content": "",
  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nSearch for all calls to play_fight_animation and analyze their context\nto find which one handles the brick throwing.\n\nThe brick+window action is:\n- Item 4 (brick) + Hotspot 294 (window) in Room 7\n\nApproach: Find calls to play_fight_animation with interesting offsets\nand trace back to see which one might be for brick throwing.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport struct\n\nwith open('files/JUEGO.EXE', 'rb') as f:\n    exe = f.read()\n\n# File offset to memory address conversion\ndef file_to_mem(f_off):\n    return f_off - 0x3200\n\ndef mem_to_file(m_addr):\n    return m_addr + 0x3200\n\n# Known animation offsets from search_brick_throw.py\nanim_offsets = {\n    0x2207FA: \"fight_animation (main_game_loop)\",\n    0x2D5B98: \"animation_1\",\n    0x1F7274: \"animation_2\", \n    0x204830: \"animation_3\",\n    0x17C03C: \"animation_4\",\n    0x186DBC: \"animation_5\",\n    0x1AB1DC: \"animation_6\",\n    0x2E5CF6: \"animation_7\",\n    0x182A56: \"animation_8\",\n    0x1ADFD2: \"animation_9\",\n    0x1B02D4: \"animation_10\",\n}\n\n# Find ALL calls to play_fight_animation (0x26420)\nprint(\"Finding all calls to play_fight_animation...\")\n\ncalls = []\n# Look for E8 xx xx xx xx pattern (CALL rel32)\nfor i in range(len(exe) - 5):\n    if exe[i] == 0xE8:\n        rel32 = struct.unpack('&lt;i', exe[i+1:i+5])[0]\n        target = file_to_mem(i+5) + rel32\n        if target == 0x26420:  # play_fight_animation\n            mem_addr = file_to_mem(i)\n            # Get the MOV EAX, offset instruction before the call\n            # Usually: MOV EAX, imm32 (B8 xx xx xx xx) a few bytes before\n            for back in range(1, 50):\n                if i &gt;= back and exe[i-back] == 0xB8:\n                    anim_offset = struct.unpack('&lt;I', exe[i-back+1:i-back+5])[0]\n                    if anim_offset in anim_offsets:\n                        calls.append((mem_addr, anim_offset, anim_offsets[anim_offset], i-back))\n                        break\n                    elif 0x100000 &lt;= anim_offset &lt;= 0x400000:  # Reasonable ALFRED.7 range\n                        calls.append((mem_addr, anim_offset, \"unknown\", i-back))\n                        break\n\nprint(f\"Found {len(calls)} calls with animation offsets:\")\nfor call_addr, offset, name, file_off in sorted(calls, key=lambda x: x[0]):\n    print(f\"  0x{call_addr:05X}: offset 0x{offset:06X} ({name})\")\n    # Show function context\n    # Look back to find PUSH 0x28 (function prologue indicator)\n    start = file_off - 200\n    if start &lt; 0:\n        start = 0\n    context = exe[start:file_off]\n    # Find any CMP or test for hotspot/item values\n    for j in range(len(context) - 2):\n        # CMP with immediate\n        if context[j:j+2] == b'\\x3D\\x26' and j+4 &lt;= len(context):\n            val = struct.unpack('&lt;H', context[j+1:j+3])[0]\n            if 0x100 &lt;= val &lt;= 0x200:\n                print(f\"    -&gt; CMP EAX, 0x{val:04X} at file 0x{start+j+0x3200:05X}\")\n        if context[j:j+3] == b'\\x81\\xFB\\x26':\n            val = struct.unpack('&lt;H', context[j+2:j+4])[0]\n            if 0x100 &lt;= val &lt;= 0x200:\n                print(f\"    -&gt; CMP EBX, 0x{val:04X} at file 0x{start+j+0x3200:05X}\")\n",
  "toolCallResult": null
}

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Analyze LOGCPU2.TXT to find unique addresses and interesting patterns.\"\"\"\nimport re\nfrom collections import defaultdict\n\nlog_path = '/Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/LOGCPU2.TXT'\n\n# Collect all addresses and their frequency\naddrs = defaultdict(lambda: {'count': 0, 'first_line': 0, 'last_line': 0, 'example': ''})\n\nwith open(log_path, 'r') as f:\n    for line_num, line in enumerate(f, 1):\n        # Match address at start: \"0160:001F2B86\"\n        m = re.match(r'([0-9A-Fa-f]+):([0-9A-Fa-f]+)\\s+(\\S+)', line)\n        if m:\n            seg = m.group(1)\n            off = m.group(2)\n            instr = m.group(3)\n            full = f\"{seg}:{off}\"\n            if addrs[full]['count'] == 0:\n                addrs[full]['first_line'] = line_num\n                addrs[full]['example'] = line.strip()[:100]\n            addrs[full]['count'] += 1\n            addrs[full]['last_line'] = line_num\n\nprint(f\"Total unique addresses: {len(addrs)}\")\n\n# Show addresses by first appearance (chronological)\nprint(\"\\n=== Addresses by first appearance (looking for animation code) ===\")\nsorted_by_first = sorted(addrs.items(), key=lambda x: x[1]['first_line'])\n\n# Skip the first few (idle loop)\nidle_addrs = {'0160:001F2BB0', '0160:001EB274', '0160:001DD000', '0160:001F2B86'}\n\nprint(\"\\nNon-idle addresses (first appearance order):\")\nfor addr, info in sorted_by_first:\n    if addr not in idle_addrs:\n        off = int(addr.split(':')[1], 16)\n        # Calculate possible Ghidra address (subtract 0x1CC000)\n        ghidra = off - EAX values that look like file offsets\nprint(\"\\n\\n=== Searching for ALFRED.7 offsets in registers ===\")\nwith open(log_path, 'r') as f:\n    for line_num, line in enumerate(f, 1):\n        # Look for EAX values in range 0x100000 - {
  "invocationMessage": "Creating [](file:///Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/extract_fight_anims.py)",
  "pastTenseMessage": "Created [](file:///Users/gabriel/Desktop/source/alfredtools/extract_fight_anims.py)",
  "isConfirmed": {
    "type": 1
  },
  "content": "",
  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nExtract all animation frames from ALFRED.7 at the known offsets used by play_fight_animation.\n\nKnown animation offsets (from search_brick_throw.py):\n  0x2207FA - fight animation (main game loop)\n  0x2D5B98 - animation 1\n  0x1F7274 - animation 2\n  0x204830 - animation 3\n  0x17C03C - animation 4\n  0x186DBC - animation 5\n  0x1AB1DC - animation 6\n  0x2E5CF6 - animation 7\n  0x182A56 - animation 8\n  0x1ADFD2 - animation 9\n  0x1B02D4 - animation 10\n\nThe play_fight_animation function signature (from Ghidra):\n- Uses file_seek to position\n- Uses file_read to load data\n- Has parameters for width, height, frame count on the stack\n\"\"\"\n\nimport struct\nimport os\nfrom PIL import Image\n\n# ALFRED.7 animation offsets from code\nANIMATION_OFFSETS = {\n    0x2207FA: \"fight_anim_main\",\n    0x2D5B98: \"anim_1\",\n    0x1F7274: \"anim_2\",\n    0x204830: \"anim_3\",\n    0x17C03C: \"anim_4\",\n    0x186DBC: \"anim_5\",\n    0x1AB1DC: \"anim_6\",\n    0x2E5CF6: \"anim_7\",\n    0x182A56: \"anim_8\",\n    0x1ADFD2: \"anim_9\",\n    0x1B02D4: \"anim_10\",\n}\n\n# ALFRED.7 file size is 3,571,728 bytes\nALFRED7_SIZE = 3571728\n\ndef load_palette():\n    \"\"\"Load the default VGA palette (grayscale for now)\"\"\"\n    palette = []\n    for i in range(256):\n        palette.extend([i, i, i])\n    return palette\n\ndef try_extract_animation(data, offset, name, output_dir):\n    \"\"\"Try to extract animation frames at the given offset\"\"\"\n    print(f\"\\n=== Extracting {name} at offset 0x{offset:06X} ===\")\n    \n    if offset &gt;= len(data):\n        print(f\"  Offset beyond file size!\")\n        return\n    \n    # Show raw data at offset\n    print(f\"  First 64 bytes at offset:\")\n    preview = data[offset:offset+64]\n    hex_str = ' '.join(f'{b:02X}' for b in preview)\n    print(f\"  {hex_str}\")\n    \n    # Try to interpret as animation header\n    # Common formats might have: width, height, frame_count at the start\n    # Let's try different interpretations\n    \n    # Try 1: Assume first bytes are width/height/framecount (16-bit each)\n    if offset + 6 &lt;= len(data):\n        w1 = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[offset:offset+2])[0]\n        h1 = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[offset+2:offset+4])[0]\n        f1 = struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[offset+4:offset+6])[0]\n        print(f\"  Interpretation 1 (WxH, frames): {w1}x{h1}, {f1} frames\")\n        \n        # If dimensions look reasonable, try to extract\n        if 10 &lt;= w1 &lt;= 320 and 10 &lt;= h1 &lt;= 200 and 1 &lt;= f1 &lt;= 20:\n            frame_size = w1 * h1\n            total_size = frame_size * f1\n            if offset + 6 + total_size &lt;= len(data):\n                print(f\"  -&gt; Looks plausible! Frame size {frame_size}, total {total_size}\")\n                try_save_frames(data, offset + 6, w1, h1, f1, name, output_dir)\n    \n    # Try 2: Assume raw pixel data starts immediately (no header)\n    # Common frame sizes: 48x48, 64x64, 32x32, etc.\n    for w, h in [(48, 48), (64, 64), (32, 32), (40, 40), (60, 60), (80, 80)]:\n        # Try 4 frames\n        frame_size = w * h\n        total = frame_size * 4\n        if offset + total &lt;= len(data):\n            try_save_frames(data, offset, w, h, 4, f\"{name}_{w}x{h}\", output_dir)\n\ndef try_save_frames(data, offset, width, height, num_frames, name, output_dir):\n    \"\"\"Save animation frames as PNG\"\"\"\n    palette = load_palette()\n    \n    frame_size = width * height\n    \n    for i in range(num_frames):\n        frame_offset = offset + i * frame_size\n        if frame_offset + frame_size &gt; len(data):\n            print(f\"  Frame {i}: out of bounds\")\n            break\n        \n        frame_data = data[frame_offset:frame_offset + frame_size]\n        \n        # Create image\n        img = Image.new('P', (width, height))\n        img.putpalette(palette)\n        img.putdata(frame_data)\n        \n        # Save\n        subdir = os.path.join(output_dir, name)\n        os.makedirs(subdir, exist_ok=True)\n        img.save(os.path.join(subdir, f\"frame_{i:02d}.png\"))\n    \n    print(f\"  Saved {num_frames} frames to {subdir}\")\n\ndef main():\n    alfred7_path = 'files/ALFRED.7'\n    output_dir = 'output_fight_anims'\n    \n    with open(alfred7_path, 'rb') as f:\n        data = f.read()\n    \n    print(f\"ALFRED.7 size: {len(data)} bytes\")\n    os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)\n    \n    # Extract all known animation offsets\n    for offset, name in sorted(ANIMATION_OFFSETS.items()):\n        try_extract_animation(data, offset, name, output_dir)\n\nif __name__ == '__main__':\n    main()\n",

}

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Find the brick+window combo entry in the item combo table.\"\"\"\n\nimport struct\n\nwith open(\"files/JUEGO.EXE\", \"rb\") as f:\n    data = f.read()\n\n# Search for brick (item 4) + window (hotspot 294) pattern\nbrick = 4\nwindow = 294\n\nprint(f\"Searching for brick (item {brick}) + window (hotspot {window}) combo...\")\nprint(f\"File size: {len(data)} bytes\")\nprint()\n\nfor offset in range(0x4B000, 0x4C000):\n    if offset + 8 &gt; len(data):\n        break\n    item1, item2, func = struct.unpack(\"&lt;HHI\", data[offset:offset+8])\n    if (item1 == brick and item2 == window) or (item1 == window and item2 == brick):\n        print(f\"Found at file offset 0x{offset:05X}:\")\n        print(f\"  item1={item1}, item2={item2}, func=0x{func:08X}\")\n        print(f\"  Memory addr ~= 0x{offset + 0x10000 - 0x11000 + 0x10000:05X}\")\n        # Show surrounding entries\n        print(f\"  Context bytes: {data[offset-16:offset+24].hex()}\")\n        print()\n\nprint(\"\\nLooking at entire combo table (0x48118 memory addr):\")\n# The table starts at memory 0x48118\n# File offset calculation: MZ+LE header ~0x11000, so 0x48118 - 0x10000 = 0x38118? \n# Or maybe different. Let's search for the table structure.\n\n# Search for sequences where multiple valid entries appear\nprint(\"\\nScanning for table structure (looking for terminator FFFF)...\")\nfor base in range(0x37000, 0x40000, 0x100):\n    count = 0\n    has_294 = False\n    for i in range(100):\n        off = base + i * 8\n        if off + 8 &gt; len(data):\n            break\n        item1, item2, func = struct.unpack(\"&lt;HHI\", data[off:off+8])\n        if item1 == 0xFFFF:\n            if count &gt; 5 and has_294:\n                print(f\"  Table candidate at 0x{base:05X}: {count} entries before terminator\")\n            break\n        # Check if entry looks valid (small hotspot/item IDs, function in code range)\n        if item1 &lt; 500 and item2 &lt; 500 and 0x10000 &lt; func &lt; 0x40000:\n            count += 1\n            if item1 == 294 or item2 == 294:\n                has_294 = True\n",

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Dump the hotspot action table at 0x47bf0 (6-byte entries).\"\"\"\n\nimport struct\n\nwith open(\"files/JUEGO.EXE\", \"rb\") as f:\n    data = f.read()\n\n# Memory address 0x47bf0 -&gt; file offset\n# Need to find the correct mapping\n# The combo table at mem 0x48118 was found at file 0x4B320\n# So offset = 0x4B320 - 0x48118 = 0x3208 (file_offset = mem_addr + 0x3208)\n# Or the other way: mem_addr = file_offset - 0x3208\n\n# So 0x47bf0 -&gt; file offset 0x47bf0 + 0x3208 = 0x4ADF8\nfile_offset = 0x47bf0 + 0x3208  # Hmm that doesn't seem right\n\n# Let me try: from combo table mem 0x48118 at file 0x4B320\n# mem 0x48118 + X = file 0x4B320\n# X = 0x4B320 - 0x48118 = 0x3208\n# So for hotspot table at mem 0x47bf0:\n# file = 0x47bf0 + 0x3208 = 0x4ADF8\n\nprint(\"Hotspot action table (mem 0x47bf0):\")\nprint(\"Format: 6 bytes per entry [hotspot_extra_id (word), function_ptr (dword)]\")\nprint()\n\n# Actually, let me calculate this differently\n# File offset 0x4B320 corresponds to memory 0x48118\n# file_offset - 0x3208 = mem_addr\n# OR: file_offset = mem_addr + 0x3208\n\n# For mem 0x47bf0:\nfile_offset = 0x47bf0 + 0x3208\nprint(f\"Calculated file offset: 0x{file_offset:05X}\")\nprint()\n\n# Let's verify by looking for -1 (0xFFFF) terminator\nfor i in range(200):\n    off = file_offset + i * 6\n    if off + 6 &gt; len(data):\n        break\n    hotspot_id, func_ptr = struct.unpack(\"&lt;HI\", data[off:off+6])\n    if hotspot_id == 0xFFFF:\n        print(f\"Entry {i:3d}: TERMINATOR at file offset 0x{off:05X}\")\n        break\n    print(f\"Entry {i:3d} (0x{off:05X}): hotspot_id={hotspot_id:5d} (0x{hotspot_id:04X}), func=0x{func_ptr:08X}\")\n    \n    # Check for window (294)\n    if hotspot_id == 294:\n        print(f\"  ^^^ WINDOW HOTSPOT (294) ^^^\")\n\nprint()\nprint(\"\\nAlternate calculation - searching for table start:\")\n# Let me search for the pattern of 6-byte entries that end in FFFF\n\nfor base in range(0x3A000, 0x4C000, 0x10):\n    # Check if this looks like the start of the table\n    # First entry should have small hotspot ID and valid function\n    if base + 6 &gt; len(data):\n        break\n    hid, func = struct.unpack(\"&lt;HI\", data[base:base+6])\n    if 250 &lt; hid &lt; 300 and 0x10000 &lt; func &lt; 0x30000:\n        # Check next few entries too\n        valid = True\n        for j in range(1, 5):\n            off = base + j * 6\n            if off + 6 &gt; len(data):\n                valid = False\n                break\n            h, f = struct.unpack(\"&lt;HI\", data[off:off+6])\n            if h != 0xFFFF and (h &gt; 500 or f &lt; 0x10000 or f &gt; 0x40000):\n                valid = False\n                break\n        if valid:\n            print(f\"Potential table at file 0x{base:05X} (mem 0x{base - 0x3208:05X}):\")\n            for j in range(10):\n                off = base + j * 6\n                h, f = struct.unpack(\"&lt;HI\", data[off:off+6])\n                if h == 0xFFFF:\n                    print(f\"  [{j}] TERMINATOR\")\n                    break\n                print(f\"  [{j}] hotspot={h}, func=0x{f:08X}\")\n",
  "toolCallResult": null
}

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Search for the hotspot action table in JUEGO.EXE\"\"\"\n\nimport struct\n\nwith open(\"files/JUEGO.EXE\", \"rb\") as f:\n    data = f.read()\n\n# The table is at memory 0x47bf0\n# Looking for sequential hotspot IDs 261, 262, 263...\n\n# From the previous dump, we found potential entry at 0x4B070:\n# hotspot=261, func=0x00010D76\n\n# Let's search for that exact pattern\ntarget = struct.pack(\"&lt;HI\", 261, 0x10D76)\nprint(f\"Searching for pattern: {target.hex()}\")\n\nfor i in range(len(data) - len(target)):\n    if data[i:i+len(target)] == target:\n        print(f\"Found at file offset 0x{i:05X}\")\n        # Dump the table\n        print(\"\\nTable dump:\")\n        for j in range(50):\n            off = i + j * 6\n            if off + 6 &gt; len(data):\n                break\n            hid, func = struct.unpack(\"&lt;HI\", data[off:off+6])\n            if hid == 0xFFFF:\n                print(f\"  [{j:3d}] TERMINATOR\")\n                break\n            marker = \" *** WINDOW ***\" if hid == 294 else \"\"\n            print(f\"  [{j:3d}] hotspot={hid:4d}, func=0x{func:08X}{marker}\")\n        \n        # Calculate memory-to-file mapping\n        mem_addr = 0x47bf0\n        file_off = i\n        delta = file_off - mem_addr\n        print(f\"\\nFile offset 0x{file_off:05X} - mem addr 0x{mem_addr:05X} = delta 0x{delta:05X}\")\n        break\n",
  "toolCallResult": null
}

data[e_lfanew:e_lfanew+2] == b\"LE\":\n    print(\"LE signature found\")\n    \n    # LE header structure (partial):\n    # +0x40: Object table offset (from LE header start)\n    # +0x44: Object count\n    # +0x80: Object page table offset\n    # +0x84: Number of pages\n    # +0xAC: Data pages offset (from start of file)\n    \n    obj_tbl_off = struct.unpack(\"&lt;I\", data[e_lfanew+0x40:e_lfanew+0x44])[0]\n    obj_count = struct.unpack(\"&lt;I\", data[e_lfanew+0x44:e_lfanew+0x48])[0]\n    page_map_off = struct.unpack(\"&lt;I\", data[e_lfanew+0x48:e_lfanew+0x4C])[0]\n    data_pages_off = struct.unpack(\"&lt;I\", data[e_lfanew+0x80:e_lfanew+0x84])[0]\n    \n    print(f\"Object table offset: 0x{obj_tbl_off:04X} (from LE header)\")\n    print(f\"Object count: {obj_count}\")\n    print(f\"Page map offset: 0x{page_map_off:04X} (from LE header)\")\n    print(f\"Data pages offset: 0x{data_pages_off:04X} (from file start)\")\n    \n    # Object table is at e_lfanew + obj_tbl_off\n    obj_tbl = e_lfanew + obj_tbl_off\n    print(f\"\\nObject table at file offset 0x{obj_tbl:04X}\")\n    \n    # Each object entry is 24 bytes\n    for i in range(min(obj_count, 4)):\n        off = obj_tbl + i * 24\n        virt_size = struct.unpack(\"&lt;I\", data[off:off+4])[0]\n        base_addr = struct.unpack(\"&lt;I\", data[off+4:off+8])[0]\n        flags = struct.unpack(\"&lt;I\", data[off+8:off+12])[0]\n        page_map_idx = struct.unpack(\"&lt;I\", data[off+12:off+16])[0]\n        page_count = struct.unpack(\"&lt;I\", data[off+16:off+20])[0]\n        print(f\"  Object {i}: base=0x{base_addr:08X}, size=0x{virt_size:08X}, pages={page_count}, map_idx={page_map_idx}\")\n\nprint()\nprint(\"=\" * 60)\nprint(\"SUMMARY:\")\nprint(\"=\" * 60)\n\n# The key insight: code is at file offset that maps to memory 0x10000\n# Based on Ghidra segments: .object1 is 0x10000-0x3E096\n# Let's calculate: to get file offset from code address 0x116F5\n# We need to know the data pages offset for object 1\n\n# From the objects: object1 starts at base 0x10000, map_idx tells us page offset\n# Page size is typically 4096 bytes in LE format\n\n# Let me look for known code pattern at 0x116F5\n# We know the function at 0x116F5 handles hotspot 294 (window)\n\n# Actually, let's just look at the data pages offset\n# The raw code starts at data_pages_off in the file\n# Code addresses are relative to 0x10000\n\nprint()\nprint(\"For function at memory 0x116F5:\")\ncode_base = 0x10000\nfunc_addr = 0x116F5\noffset_from_base = func_addr - code_base\nprint(f\"  Offset from code base: 0x{offset_from_base:05X}\")\nprint(f\"  File offset = data_pages_offset + {offset_from_base}\")\n\n# data_pages_off should give us the start of raw data\n# Let me verify with known function start\n# Function at 0x10442 (game_initialization from Ghidra)\n# Has known signature: PUSH 0x34\nknown_func = 0x10442\nknown_off = known_func - code_base\nprint(f\"\\nVerifying with known function at 0x{known_func:05X}:\")\n\n# Try different page offsets to find the right one\nfor test_off in [data_pages_off, 0x1000, 0x600, 0x500, 0x400]:\n    file_off = test_off + known_off\n    if file_off &lt; len(data):\n        byte = data[file_off]\n        # PUSH imm8 is 0x6A\n        if byte == 0x6A:\n            print(f\"  With data offset 0x{test_off:04X}: file_off=0x{file_off:05X} -&gt; byte 0x{byte:02X} (PUSH!) ✓\")\n            \n            # Now find the window handler at 0x116F5\n            window_file_off = test_off + (0x116F5 - code_base)\n            print(f\"\\n  Window handler (0x116F5) file offset: 0x{window_file_off:05X}\")\n            print(f\"  First 32 bytes: {data[window_file_off:window_file_off+32].hex()}\")\n        else:\n            print(f\"  With data offset 0x{test_off:04X}: file_off=0x{file_off:05X} -&gt; byte 0x{byte:02X}\")\n",

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Disassemble the window handler at 0x116F5\"\"\"\n\nimport struct\n\nwith open(\"files/JUEGO.EXE\", \"rb\") as f:\n    data = f.read()\n\n# Code mapping: file_offset = 0x14200 + (mem_addr - 0x10000)\ndef mem_to_file(mem_addr):\n    return 0x14200 + (mem_addr - 0x10000)\n\n# Window handler at 0x116F5\nwindow_handler = 0x116F5\nfile_off = mem_to_file(window_handler)\n\nprint(f\"Window handler at mem 0x{window_handler:05X}\")\nprint(f\"File offset: 0x{file_off:05X}\")\nprint()\n\n# Read bytes and attempt simple disassembly\ncode = data[file_off:file_off+100]\nprint(f\"First 100 bytes (hex):\")\nfor i in range(0, len(code), 16):\n    hex_str = \" \".join(f\"{b:02X}\" for b in code[i:i+16])\n    print(f\"  {window_handler + i:05X}: {hex_str}\")\n\nprint()\nprint(\"Simple analysis:\")\n# Look at first few instructions\n# PUSH imm8 = 6A xx\n# PUSH imm32 = 68 xx xx xx xx\n# CALL rel32 = E8 xx xx xx xx\n# RET = C3\n# CMP = 83 or 3D\n# JZ/JNZ = 74/75\n\ni = 0\nwhile i &lt; 50:\n    opcode = code[i]\n    mem_addr = window_handler + i\n    if opcode == 0x6A:  # PUSH imm8\n        print(f\"  {mem_addr:05X}: PUSH 0x{code[i+1]:02X}\")\n        i += 2\n    elif opcode == 0x68:  # PUSH imm32\n        val = struct.unpack(\"&lt;I\", code[i+1:i+5])[0]\n        print(f\"  {mem_addr:05X}: PUSH 0x{val:08X}\")\n        i += 5\n    elif opcode == 0xE8:  # CALL rel32\n        rel = struct.unpack(\"&lt;i\", code[i+1:i+5])[0]\n        target = mem_addr + 5 + rel\n        print(f\"  {mem_addr:05X}: CALL 0x{target:08X}\")\n        i += 5\n    elif opcode == 0xC3:  # RET\n        print(f\"  {mem_addr:05X}: RET\")\n        i += 1\n        break\n    elif opcode in [0x50, 0x51, 0x52, 0x53, 0x54, 0x55, 0x56, 0x57]:\n        regs = [\"EAX\", \"ECX\", \"EDX\", \"EBX\", \"ESP\", \"EBP\", \"ESI\", \"EDI\"]\n        print(f\"  {mem_addr:05X}: PUSH {regs[opcode - 0x50]}\")\n        i += 1\n    elif opcode in [0x58, 0x59, 0x5A, 0x5B, 0x5C, 0x5D, 0x5E, 0x5F]:\n        regs = [\"EAX\", \"ECX\", \"EDX\", \"EBX\", \"ESP\", \"EBP\", \"ESI\", \"EDI\"]\n        print(f\"  {mem_addr:05X}: POP {regs[opcode - 0x58]}\")\n        i += 1\n    elif opcode == 0x83:  # CMP/ADD/SUB r/m, imm8\n        modrm = code[i+1]\n        op = (modrm &gt;&gt; 3) &amp; 7\n        ops = [\"ADD\", \"OR\", \"ADC\", \"SBB\", \"AND\", \"SUB\", \"XOR\", \"CMP\"]\n        print(f\"  {mem_addr:05X}: {ops[op]} ??? 0x{code[i+2]:02X}\")\n        i += 3\n    elif opcode == 0x74:  # JZ rel8\n        rel = struct.unpack(\"&lt;b\", bytes([code[i+1]]))[0]\n        target = mem_addr + 2 + rel\n        print(f\"  {mem_addr:05X}: JZ 0x{target:05X}\")\n        i += 2\n    elif opcode == 0x75:  # JNZ rel8\n        rel = struct.unpack(\"&lt;b\", bytes([code[i+1]]))[0]\n        target = mem_addr + 2 + rel\n        print(f\"  {mem_addr:05X}: JNZ 0x{target:05X}\")\n        i += 2\n    elif opcode == 0x31:  # XOR r, r/m\n        print(f\"  {mem_addr:05X}: XOR ...\")\n        i += 2\n    elif opcode == 0x33:  # XOR r, r/m\n        print(f\"  {mem_addr:05X}: XOR ...\")\n        i += 2\n    elif opcode == 0x89:  # MOV r/m, r\n        print(f\"  {mem_addr:05X}: MOV ...\")\n        i += 2  # could be more depending on modrm\n    elif opcode == 0xA1:  # MOV EAX, [imm32]\n        addr = struct.unpack(\"&lt;I\", code[i+1:i+5])[0]\n        print(f\"  {mem_addr:05X}: MOV EAX, [0x{addr:08X}]\")\n        i += 5\n    elif opcode == 0xB8:  # MOV EAX, imm32\n        val = struct.unpack(\"&lt;I\", code[i+1:i+5])[0]\n        print(f\"  {mem_addr:05X}: MOV EAX, 0x{val:08X}\")\n        i += 5\n    elif opcode == 0x81:  # CMP/etc r/m, imm32\n        print(f\"  {mem_addr:05X}: CMP/etc ...\")\n        i += 6\n    else:\n        print(f\"  {mem_addr:05X}: ??? opcode 0x{opcode:02X}\")\n        i += 1\n\nprint()\nprint(\"Also checking nearby handlers:\")\n# Handler 292 at 0x1161D\n# Handler 293 at 0x1163A\nfor name, addr in [(\"292\", 0x1161D), (\"293\", 0x1163A), (\"295\", 0x118CC)]:\n    fo = mem_to_file(addr)\n    print(f\"\\nHandler {name} at 0x{addr:05X} (file 0x{fo:05X}):\")\n    code = data[fo:fo+20]\n    print(f\"  Bytes: {code.hex()}\")\n",

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nSearch JUEGO.EXE for 4-frame animations, particularly the brick throwing animation.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport struct\n\ndef file_to_mem(file_off):\n    \"\"\"Convert file offset to memory address\"\"\"\n    return file_off - 0x14200 + 0x10000\n\ndef mem_to_file(mem_addr):\n    \"\"\"Convert memory address to file offset\"\"\"\n    return 0x14200 + (mem_addr - 0x10000)\n\ndef read_word(data, off):\n    return struct.unpack('&lt;H', data[off:off+2])[0]\n\ndef read_dword(data, off):\n    return struct.unpack('&lt;I', data[off:off+4])[0]\n\nwith open('files/JUEGO.EXE', 'rb') as f:\n    data = f.read()\n\nprint(\"=\" * 70)\nprint(\"SEARCHING FOR 4-FRAME ANIMATION PATTERNS IN JUEGO.EXE\")\nprint(\"=\" * 70)\n\n# 1. Search for CALL to play_fight_animation (0x26420)\nprint(\"\\n[1] Searching for CALL 0x26420 (play_fight_animation)...\")\ntarget_addr = 0x26420\n# E8 XX XX = CALL rel16\nfor i in range(0x14200, len(data) - 3):\n    if data[i] == 0xE8:  # CALL rel16\n        rel = struct.unpack('&lt;h', data[i+1:i+3])[0]  # signed 16-bit\n        dest = file_to_mem(i) + 3 + rel\n        if dest == target_addr:\n            mem = file_to_mem(i)\n            print(f\"  Found CALL 0x26420 at file 0x{i:05X} (mem 0x{mem:05X})\")\n            # Show context before the call\n            ctx_start = max(0, i - 30)\n            print(f\"    Context before: {data[ctx_start:i].hex()}\")\n\n# 2. Search for PUSH 4 (6A 04) - immediate byte push\nprint(\"\\n[2] Searching for PUSH 4 (6A 04) in handler region 0x10D00-0x15000...\")\nfor mem_addr in range(0x10D00, 0x15000):\n    fo = mem_to_file(mem_addr)\n    if fo &lt; len(data) - 10:\n        if data[fo] == 0x6A and data[fo+1] == 0x04:\n            # Look for context - is this near animation-related code?\n            ctx = data[fo-20:fo+20]\n            print(f\"  0x{mem_addr:05X}: PUSH 4  context: {ctx.hex()}\")\n\n# 3. Search for large ALFRED.7 offsets being pushed (MOV AX, imm16 or PUSH imm16)\nprint(\"\\n[3] Searching for ALFRED.7 offset loads (0x1XXXXX-0x3XXXXX range)...\")\n# Look for patterns like:\n#   B8 XX XX (MOV AX, imm16) followed by more loads\n#   68 XX XX XX XX (PUSH imm32) - unlikely in 16-bit code\n#   C7 XX XX XX XX (MOV word ptr, imm16)\n\n# Check the known fight animation area for comparison\nprint(\"\\n  Known fight animation at 0x2207FA (71x102, 11 frames)\")\nprint(\"  Checking how it's loaded...\")\n\n# Search for 0x2207 or 0x07FA patterns (split word access)\nfor i in range(0x14200, len(data) - 4):\n    # MOV reg, 0x2207 or 0x07FA\n    if data[i] == 0xB8 or data[i] == 0xBB or data[i] == 0xB9:  # MOV AX/BX/CX, imm16\n        val = read_word(data, i+1)\n        if val == 0x2207 or val == 0x07FA or val == 0x220:\n            mem = file_to_mem(i)\n            print(f\"  0x{mem:05X}: MOV reg, 0x{val:04X}\")\n\n# 4. Look specifically at window handler 0x116F5\nprint(\"\\n[4] Analyzing window handler at 0x116F5...\")\nfo = mem_to_file(0x116F5)\nprint(f\"  File offset: 0x{fo:05X}\")\nprint(f\"  First 100 bytes:\")\nfor off in range(0, 100, 16):\n    chunk = data[fo+off:fo+off+16]\n    hex_str = ' '.join(f'{b:02X}' for b in chunk)\n    print(f\"    0x{0x116F5+off:05X}: {hex_str}\")\n\n# 5. Search in broader region for animation dimension patterns\nprint(\"\\n[5] Searching for small dimension patterns (30-60 pixel range)...\")\n# Animation typically: width, height, frame_count pushed before call\n# PUSH width; PUSH height; PUSH frame_count; CALL render_func\n\nfor mem_addr in range(0x10D00, 0x18000):\n    fo = mem_to_file(mem_addr)\n    if fo &lt; len(data) - 20:\n        # Pattern: 6A XX 6A XX 6A 04 (three PUSH imm8 with last being 4)\n        if (data[fo] == 0x6A and data[fo+2] == 0x6A and \n            data[fo+4] == 0x6A and data[fo+5] == 0x04):\n            w = data[fo+1]\n            h = data[fo+3]\n            if 20 &lt;= w &lt;= 100 and 20 &lt;= h &lt;= 100:\n                print(f\"  0x{mem_addr:05X}: PUSH {w}; PUSH {h}; PUSH 4  (potential anim)\")\n\n# 6. Search for brick-related code patterns\nprint(\"\\n[6] Searching for item IDs near animation code...\")\n# Brick item ID might be specific - look for comparison patterns\n# CMP AL, XX or CMP [mem], XX where XX could be brick ID\n\n# Look at brick+window combo handler area (around 0x127B2 from context)\nprint(\"\\n  Brick combo handler area (0x127B2-0x12900):\")\nfor mem_addr in range(0x127B2, 0x12900, 16):\n    fo = mem_to_file(mem_addr)\n    chunk = data[fo:fo+16]\n    hex_str = ' '.join(f'{b:02X}' for b in chunk)\n    \n    # Disassemble key opcodes\n    disasm = []\n    i = 0\n    while i &lt; 16:\n        b = chunk[i]\n        if b == 0x6A:  # PUSH imm8\n            disasm.append(f\"PUSH {chunk[i+1]:02X}\")\n            i += 2\n        elif b == 0xE8:  # CALL rel16\n            if i + 2 &lt; 16:\n                rel = struct.unpack('&lt;h', chunk[i+1:i+3])[0]\n                dest = mem_addr + i + 3 + rel\n                disasm.append(f\"CALL {dest:04X}\")\n            i += 3\n        elif b == 0xB8:  # MOV AX, imm16\n            if i + 2 &lt; 16:\n                val = read_word(chunk, i+1)\n                disasm.append(f\"MOV AX,{val:04X}\")\n            i += 3\n        else:\n            i += 1\n    \n    print(f\"    0x{mem_addr:05X}: {hex_str}  {' | '.join(disasm)}\")\n\n# 7. Search the entire hotspot handler region for ALFRED.7 references\nprint(\"\\n[7] Scanning hotspot handlers (0x10D00-0x14000) for segment:offset loads...\")\n# In DOS, large file offsets are often loaded as seg:off pairs\n# Look for consecutive loads that could represent 0x2XXXXX type values\n\nfor mem_addr in range(0x10D00, 0x14000):\n    fo = mem_to_file(mem_addr)\n    if fo &lt; len(data) - 6:\n        # Look for MOV reg, high_word followed by MOV reg, low_word\n        # BA XX XX (MOV DX, imm16) - often segment\n        # B8 XX XX (MOV AX, imm16) - often offset\n        if data[fo] == 0xBA:  # MOV DX, imm16\n            seg = read_word(data, fo+1)\n            if data[fo+3] == 0xB8:  # MOV AX, imm16\n                off = read_word(data, fo+4)\n                linear = (seg &lt;&lt; 4) + off\n                if 0x100000 &lt;= linear &lt;= 0x400000:  # ALFRED.7 range\n                    print(f\"  0x{mem_addr:05X}: MOV DX,{seg:04X}; MOV AX,{off:04X} = linear 0x{linear:06X}\")\n\nprint(\"\\n[8] Looking for alternative patterns - direct offset loading...\")\n# Some code might load 32-bit values differently\n# Check for LES/LDS instructions or direct memory references\n\n# Search for specific bytes that might be frame counts near calls\nprint(\"\\n[9] Frame count search - looking for value 4 near CALL instructions...\")\nfor mem_addr in range(0x10D00, 0x15000):\n    fo = mem_to_file(mem_addr)\n    if fo &lt; len(data) - 15:\n        # Look for PUSH 4 within 10 bytes before a CALL\n        if data[fo] == 0x6A and data[fo+1] == 0x04:\n            # Check next 10 bytes for CALL\n            for j in range(2, 12):\n                if fo + j &lt; len(data) - 2 and data[fo+j] == 0xE8:\n                    rel = struct.unpack('&lt;h', data[fo+j+1:fo+j+3])[0]\n                    dest = mem_addr + j + 3 + rel\n                    if 0x20000 &lt;= dest &lt;= 0x30000:  # Likely graphics/animation code\n                        ctx_before = data[fo-10:fo]\n                        print(f\"  0x{mem_addr:05X}: PUSH 4, then CALL 0x{dest:05X}\")\n                        print(f\"    Before: {ctx_before.hex()}\")\n                    break\n\nprint(\"\\n\" + \"=\" * 70)\nprint(\"DONE\")\n",

}

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Extract the 4-frame brick throwing animation from ALFRED.7\"\"\"\n\nimport struct\nimport os\n\n# Animation parameters discovered:\n# - ALFRED.7 offset: 0x2D5B98\n# - Width: 51 pixels\n# - Height: 102 pixels  \n# - Frame count: 4\n# - Compressed flag: 0 (uncompressed!)\n\nALFRED7_OFFSET = 0x2D5B98\nWIDTH = 51\nHEIGHT = 102\nFRAME_COUNT = 4\nCOMPRESSED = False  # Last push was 0\n\nFRAME_SIZE = WIDTH * HEIGHT\n\nwith open(\"files/ALFRED.7\", \"rb\") as f:\n    f.seek(ALFRED7_OFFSET)\n    anim_data = f.read(FRAME_SIZE * FRAME_COUNT + 100)  # Read a bit extra\n\nprint(f\"Brick throwing animation:\")\nprint(f\"  ALFRED.7 offset: 0x{ALFRED7_OFFSET:06X}\")\nprint(f\"  Width: {WIDTH}\")\nprint(f\"  Height: {HEIGHT}\")\nprint(f\"  Frames: {FRAME_COUNT}\")\nprint(f\"  Frame size: {FRAME_SIZE} bytes\")\nprint(f\"  Total size: {FRAME_SIZE * FRAME_COUNT} bytes\")\nprint()\n\n# Check first bytes\nprint(f\"First 32 bytes: {anim_data[:32].hex()}\")\nprint()\n\n# Check if it looks like raw pixel data or RLE\n# RLE patterns would have FF xx 00 sequences\nhas_rle = b'\\xff' in anim_data[:100] and anim_data[:100].count(0xFF) &gt; 5\n\nif has_rle:\n    print(\"WARNING: Data appears to be RLE compressed despite flag=0\")\n    # Let me check the pattern more carefully\n    ff_indices = [i for i, b in enumerate(anim_data[:200]) if b == 0xFF]\n    print(f\"  0xFF positions in first 200 bytes: {ff_indices[:20]}\")\nelse:\n    print(\"Data appears to be raw (uncompressed)\")\n\n# Extract frames\nos.makedirs(\"output_brick_anim\", exist_ok=True)\n\nfor frame in range(FRAME_COUNT):\n    start = frame * FRAME_SIZE\n    end = start + FRAME_SIZE\n    frame_data = anim_data[start:end]\n    \n    print(f\"\\nFrame {frame}:\")\n    print(f\"  Offset: 0x{ALFRED7_OFFSET + start:06X}\")\n    print(f\"  First 16 bytes: {frame_data[:16].hex()}\")\n    \n    # Count unique values\n    unique = len(set(frame_data))\n    print(f\"  Unique values: {unique}\")\n    \n    # Common values\n    from collections import Counter\n    common = Counter(frame_data).most_common(5)\n    print(f\"  Most common: {common}\")\n    \n    # Save raw frame data\n    with open(f\"output_brick_anim/frame_{frame}_raw.bin\", \"wb\") as f:\n        f.write(frame_data)\n    \n    # Create PPM image (grayscale for now - need palette)\n    ppm_data = \"P6\\n{} {}\\n255\\n\".format(WIDTH, HEIGHT)\n    with open(f\"output_brick_anim/frame_{frame}.ppm\", \"wb\") as f:\n        f.write(ppm_data.encode())\n        # Convert palette indices to grayscale RGB\n        for b in frame_data:\n            # 0xFF is transparent, use black\n            if b == 0xFF:\n                f.write(bytes([0, 0, 0]))\n            else:\n                # Use palette index as grayscale\n                f.write(bytes([b * 4, b * 4, b * 4]))\n\nprint()\nprint(f\"Saved {FRAME_COUNT} frames to output_brick_anim/\")\nprint(\"Note: PPM images use grayscale mapping (need actual palette for colors)\")\n",

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Extract and decompress the 4-frame brick throwing animation from ALFRED.7\"\"\"\n\nimport struct\nimport os\n\n# Animation parameters discovered:\n# - ALFRED.7 offset: 0x2D5B98\n# - Width: 51 pixels\n# - Height: 102 pixels  \n# - Frame count: 4\n\nALFRED7_OFFSET = 0x2D5B98\nWIDTH = 51\nHEIGHT = 102\nFRAME_COUNT = 4\nFRAME_SIZE = WIDTH * HEIGHT\n\ndef decompress_rle(data, expected_size=None):\n    \"\"\"\n    Decompress Alfred RLE format.\n    Format: [count][value] pairs, terminated by 'BUDA' marker\n    \"\"\"\n    output = []\n    i = 0\n    \n    while i &lt; len(data) - 1:\n        # Check for BUDA marker\n        if i + 4 &lt;= len(data) and data[i:i+4] == b'BUDA':\n            break\n        \n        count = data[i]\n        value = data[i + 1]\n        i += 2\n        \n        # Handle count=0 specially (might mean 256 or end)\n        if count == 0:\n            output.append(value)\n            continue\n            \n        # Write value repeated count times\n        output.extend([value] * count)\n        \n        # Check if we've reached expected size\n        if expected_size and len(output) &gt;= expected_size:\n            break\n    \n    return bytes(output)\n\ndef decompress_rle_v2(data, expected_size):\n    \"\"\"\n    Alternative interpretation: low byte=count, high byte=value in word pairs\n    \"\"\"\n    output = []\n    i = 0\n    \n    while i &lt; len(data) - 1 and len(output) &lt; expected_size:\n        # Check for BUDA marker\n        if i + 4 &lt;= len(data) and data[i:i+4] == b'BUDA':\n            break\n            \n        count = data[i]\n        value = data[i + 1]\n        i += 2\n        \n        if count == 0:\n            count = 1  # count=0 means 1 repeat\n        \n        output.extend([value] * count)\n    \n    return bytes(output[:expected_size])\n\nwith open(\"files/ALFRED.7\", \"rb\") as f:\n    f.seek(ALFRED7_OFFSET)\n    anim_data = f.read(50000)  # Read plenty of data\n\nprint(f\"Brick throwing animation:\")\nprint(f\"  ALFRED.7 offset: 0x{ALFRED7_OFFSET:06X}\")\nprint(f\"  Width: {WIDTH}\")\nprint(f\"  Height: {HEIGHT}\")\nprint(f\"  Frames: {FRAME_COUNT}\")\nprint(f\"  Frame size: {FRAME_SIZE} bytes\")\nprint(f\"  Total decompressed size: {FRAME_SIZE * FRAME_COUNT} bytes\")\nprint()\n\n# Check first bytes\nprint(f\"First 64 bytes (compressed):\")\nfor row in range(4):\n    start = row * 16\n    hex_str = \" \".join(f\"{b:02X}\" for b in anim_data[start:start+16])\n    ascii_str = \"\".join(chr(b) if 32 &lt;= b &lt; 127 else \".\" for b in anim_data[start:start+16])\n    print(f\"  {start:04X}: {hex_str}  {ascii_str}\")\n\n# Try decompression\nprint()\nprint(\"Attempting RLE decompression...\")\n\n# Decompress all data\ndecompressed = decompress_rle_v2(anim_data, FRAME_SIZE * FRAME_COUNT)\nprint(f\"Decompressed {len(decompressed)} bytes\")\n\nos.makedirs(\"output_brick_anim\", exist_ok=True)\n\n# Save decompressed data\nwith open(\"output_brick_anim/all_frames_raw.bin\", \"wb\") as f:\n    f.write(decompressed)\n\n# Extract and visualize frames\nfor frame in range(FRAME_COUNT):\n    start = frame * FRAME_SIZE\n    end = start + FRAME_SIZE\n    frame_data = decompressed[start:end]\n    \n    print(f\"\\nFrame {frame}:\")\n    print(f\"  First 16 bytes: {frame_data[:16].hex()}\")\n    \n    # Count unique values\n    unique = len(set(frame_data))\n    print(f\"  Unique values: {unique}\")\n    \n    # Common values\n    from collections import Counter\n    common = Counter(frame_data).most_common(5)\n    print(f\"  Most common: {common}\")\n    \n    # Save raw frame\n    with open(f\"output_brick_anim/frame_{frame}_raw.bin\", \"wb\") as f:\n        f.write(frame_data)\n    \n    # Create PPM image (grayscale)\n    with open(f\"output_brick_anim/frame_{frame}.ppm\", \"wb\") as f:\n        f.write(f\"P6\\n{WIDTH} {HEIGHT}\\n255\\n\".encode())\n        for b in frame_data:\n            if b == 0xFF:\n                f.write(bytes([255, 0, 255]))  # Magenta = transparent\n            else:\n                val = min(b, 63) * 4\n                f.write(bytes([val, val, val]))\n\nprint()\nprint(f\"Saved {FRAME_COUNT} frames to output_brick_anim/\")\n\n# Also look for 'BUDA' marker to see actual compressed size\nbuda_pos = anim_data.find(b'BUDA')\nif buda_pos &gt;= 0:\n    print(f\"\\nBUDA marker found at offset +0x{buda_pos:04X}\")\n    print(f\"Compressed data size: ~{buda_pos} bytes\")\n",

  "textEditContent": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Search all ALFRED files for 71x101 animation\"\"\"\n\nimport struct\nimport os\n\nfor alfred_num in [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]:\n    fname = f\"files/ALFRED.{alfred_num}\"\n    if not os.path.exists(fname):\n        continue\n    \n    with open(fname, \"rb\") as f:\n        data = f.read()\n    \n    print(f\"\\n{'='*60}\")\n    print(f\"Searching {fname} ({len(data)} bytes)\")\n    print(\"=\"*60)\n    \n    # Search for width=71 (0x47) followed by height=101 (0x65) as 16-bit LE\n    for i in range(len(data) - 10):\n        w = struct.unpack(\"&lt;H\", data[i:i+2])[0]\n        h = struct.unpack(\"&lt;H\", data[i+2:i+4])[0]\n        \n        if w == 71 and h == 101:\n            print(f\"  Found w=71, h=101 at 0x{i:06X}\")\n            print(f\"    Context: {data[i:i+20].hex()}\")\n        \n        if w == 71 and (90 &lt;= h &lt;= 110):\n            print(f\"  Found w=71, h={h} at 0x{i:06X}\")\n            print(f\"    Context: {data[i:i+20].hex()}\")\n        \n        if h == 71 and (90 &lt;= w &lt;= 110):\n            print(f\"  Found h=71, w={w} at 0x{i:06X}\")  \n            print(f\"    Context: {data[i:i+20].hex()}\")\n\n    # Also search for 71 and 101 as single bytes adjacent with 4\n    found = set()\n    for i in range(len(data) - 8):\n        chunk = data[i:i+8]\n        vals = list(chunk)\n        \n        # Look for pattern that could be: 4 frames, width 71, height 101\n        # Or: width 71, height 101, 4 frames\n        if 71 in vals and 101 in vals and 4 in vals:\n            key = i // 16  # Dedupe by 16-byte blocks\n            if key not in found:\n                found.add(key)\n                # Additional check: are 71 and 101 within 3 positions of each other?\n                idx71 = vals.index(71)\n                idx101 = vals.index(101)\n                idx4 = vals.index(4)\n                if abs(idx71 - idx101) &lt;= 3 and abs(idx71 - idx4) &lt;= 4:\n                    print(f\"  Possible header at 0x{i:06X}: {chunk.hex()} (71 at +{idx71}, 101 at +{idx101}, 4 at +{idx4})\")\n",
